table.name: Injector Scaling
table.description: Injector size constant, shown as the injector flow (g/s) the ECU assumes at the 0.3 MPa reference of Injector Flow Compensation. Cranking pulses, latency, minimum pulse and the throttle-rate transient fuel are in microseconds and do not follow it.

table.name: Injector Latency
table.description: Fixed time added to every injection pulse, by rail pressure; probably the injector opening delay.

table.name: Injector Latency Adder
table.description: Extra latency added only while an injector-driver fault (P062D / P2146) is active. No effect on a healthy car.

table.name: Injector Flow Compensation (Injectors 1/3)
table.description: Multiplier on the fuel quantity of injectors 1 and 3 by rail pressure: more pressure means more flow, so less pulse. Keep equal to Injector Flow Compensation (Injectors 2/4).

table.name: Injector Flow Compensation (Injectors 2/4)
table.description: Same as Injector Flow Compensation (Injectors 1/3) but for injectors 2 and 4 (rail pressure plus Injector 2/4 Rail Pressure Offset).

table.name: Injector Minimum Pulse Width
table.description: Shortest pulse the ECU will command; any shorter computed pulse is raised to this. Adjust for injectors with a different minimum controllable pulse.

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Trim 1
table.description: Fuel multiplier for cylinder 1 only, by fuel quantity and rpm (128 = no change), applied before the pulse is split into injections. Use it to balance individual cylinders.

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Trim 2
table.description: Fuel multiplier for cylinder 2 only, by fuel quantity and rpm (128 = no change), applied before the pulse is split into injections. Use it to balance individual cylinders.

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Trim 3
table.description: Fuel multiplier for cylinder 3 only, by fuel quantity and rpm (128 = no change), applied before the pulse is split into injections. Use it to balance individual cylinders.

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Trim 4
table.description: Fuel multiplier for cylinder 4 only, by fuel quantity and rpm (128 = no change), applied before the pulse is split into injections. Use it to balance individual cylinders.

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Multiplier 1 (Single Injection)
table.description: Fuel multiplier for injector 1 when it fires once per cycle.

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Multiplier 2 (Single Injection)
table.description: Fuel multiplier for injector 2 when it fires once per cycle.

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Multiplier 3 (Single Injection)
table.description: Fuel multiplier for injector 3 when it fires once per cycle.

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Multiplier 4 (Single Injection)
table.description: Fuel multiplier for injector 4 when it fires once per cycle.

table.name: Injector 2/4 Rail Pressure Offset
table.description: Pressure offset added to measured rail pressure before looking up Injector Flow Compensation (Injectors 2/4), by rpm and load; probably the pressure difference of the rail without the sensor.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure
table.description: Main fuel rail pressure target in normal warm running, by load and rpm. Higher pressure = better atomisation and more injector flow at the cost of pump load. Replaced by Target Rail Pressure (Pedal Released) with the pedal released.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Pedal Released)
table.description: Rail pressure target used instead of Target Rail Pressure while the accelerator is fully released (cranking or running), by coolant.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure Additive
table.description: Extra rail pressure added to Target Rail Pressure, scaled by Target Rail Pressure Additive Multiplier, only with no rail-pressure sensor faults.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure Additive Multiplier
table.description: Scaling (255 = x1.0) for Target Rail Pressure Additive, by an unidentified input and what is probably intake air temperature.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 0)
table.description: Rail pressure target in the first phase after start (combustion mode 0), by coolant and rpm.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 4, Start Delay)
table.description: Rail pressure target used in normal running mode only during a start delay before the engine counts as running.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Released)
table.description: Rail pressure target in combustion mode 3 (the phase before normal running) with the accelerator fully released, by coolant.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied)
table.description: Rail pressure target in combustion mode 3 (the phase before normal running) with the accelerator pressed, by coolant.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1)
table.description: Rail pressure target in combustion mode 1 (an early warm-up phase).

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description: AT/CVT version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1). Only used with the automatic/CVT transmission coding; no effect on a manual car.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Catalyst Heating)
table.description: Fixed rail pressure target during stratified catalyst heating (combustion mode 2).

table.name: Rail Pressure Fail-Safe Target A
table.description: Rail pressure target while an injector-driver fault (P062D / P2146) is active. No effect on a healthy car.

table.name: Rail Pressure Fail-Safe Target B
table.description: Second fail-safe rail pressure target; the lower of A and B is used when both apply. Nothing that activates it was found, so it probably never applies.

table.name: HPFP Feedforward Command
Fuel Quantity
table.scaling: us (injector pulse 0.3 MPa ref incl. latency) uint16

table.description: Open-loop high-pressure pump command (a crank angle) by fuel quantity and rpm; the pressure controller adds its correction on top. Lower angles appear to mean more pump delivery. The fuel-quantity axis is in microseconds of injector pulse, so it must be rescaled when Injector Scaling changes.

table.name: HPFP Proportional Gain
table.description: Proportional gain of the rail-pressure controller, by rpm: how hard the pump command reacts to pressure error. Higher = faster but risks oscillation.

table.name: Base Fuel Quantity Limit
table.description: Ceiling on the base fuel quantity, the stoichiometric fuel the ECU calculates from measured air before any enrichment. Its meaning in air depends on Injector Scaling. Raise it in proportion when you raise Injector Scaling, or the engine will run lean at high airflow.

table.name: HPFP Integral Step
table.description: How much the rail-pressure controller's integral term moves each 10 ms pass, toward removing a steady pressure error. Higher = faster correction, more risk of hunting.

table.name: HPFP Integral Threshold
Fuel Quantity
table.scaling: us (injector pulse 0.3 MPa ref incl. latency) uint16

table.description: Deadband of the rail-pressure integrator, by fuel quantity (microseconds of injector pulse): while the pressure error is smaller than this, the integral term holds; beyond it, it steps toward removing the error. Larger = more steady error tolerated, less hunting.

table.name: HPFP Command Minimum
table.description: Lower limit of the high-pressure pump command, a crank angle in the pump frame. The upper limit is HPFP Command Maximum Base plus HPFP Command Range, so raising this does not raise the upper limit; keep it below that.

table.name: HPFP Command Maximum Base
table.description: Base of the high-pressure pump command upper limit: the limit is this + HPFP Command Range. Raise this (or the Range) to raise the upper limit; HPFP Command Minimum does not move it.

table.name: HPFP Command Range
table.description: Range of the high-pressure pump command: the upper limit is HPFP Command Maximum Base + this, so it does not move with HPFP Command Minimum. Also used by the pump solenoid circuit monitor.

table.name: HPFP Solenoid Window Start
table.description: Start of the pump solenoid's energised window, by battery voltage and rpm, as a crank angle in the pump frame. Used whenever the engine is running.

table.name: HPFP Solenoid Window End Limit
table.description: Upper limit on the end of the pump solenoid's energised window, by battery voltage and rpm, as a crank angle.

table.name: HPFP Solenoid End Offset
table.description: Crank angle subtracted from the pump command to give the end of the solenoid's energised window, by rpm.

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Multiplier 1 (Double Injection)
table.description: Fuel multiplier for injector 1 when it fires twice per cycle (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Multiplier 1 (Triple Injection)
table.description: Fuel multiplier for injector 1 when it fires three times per cycle (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Multiplier 2 (Double Injection)
table.description: Fuel multiplier for injector 2 when it fires twice per cycle (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Multiplier 2 (Triple Injection)
table.description: Fuel multiplier for injector 2 when it fires three times per cycle (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Multiplier 3 (Double Injection)
table.description: Fuel multiplier for injector 3 when it fires twice per cycle (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Multiplier 3 (Triple Injection)
table.description: Fuel multiplier for injector 3 when it fires three times per cycle (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Multiplier 4 (Double Injection)
table.description: Fuel multiplier for injector 4 when it fires twice per cycle (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Multiplier 4 (Triple Injection)
table.description: Fuel multiplier for injector 4 when it fires three times per cycle (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Fallback)
table.description:
Rail pressure target in combustion mode 1 after a warm-up fallback has latched.
Details: When used: Used only while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set, a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch (0x081EFC) gated by cal 0x59134 bit 0. 0x165180 (read): target in combustion mode FFF8A85C = 1 while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set (else Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1)); coolant FFF88A44. Confidence: read.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Fallback, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description: AT/CVT version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Fallback).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling
table.description: Base open-loop (power enrichment) AFR target by rpm and load, used once the exhaust temperature estimate is high enough. The ECU uses the richer of this and the Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV..., AVCS...) group: to lean, edit both; to richen, either. Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor (Outside Closed Loop).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Closed, AVCS Inactive)
table.description: Open-loop AFR target for TGVs closed with AVCS not in active control, part of a blend by TGV position and AVCS state, used above Open Loop Delay Load Threshold after a delay. The ECU uses the richer of the two systems, so leaning needs both.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Closed, AVCS Active)
table.description: Open-loop AFR target for TGVs closed with AVCS in active control, part of a blend by TGV position and AVCS state, used above Open Loop Delay Load Threshold after a delay. The ECU uses the richer of the two systems, so leaning needs both.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Open, AVCS Inactive)
table.description: Open-loop AFR target for TGVs open with AVCS not in active control, part of a blend by TGV position and AVCS state, used above Open Loop Delay Load Threshold after a delay. The ECU uses the richer of the two systems, so leaning needs both.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Open, AVCS Active)
table.description: Open-loop AFR target for TGVs open with AVCS in active control, part of a blend by TGV position and AVCS state, used above Open Loop Delay Load Threshold after a delay. The ECU uses the richer of the two systems, so leaning needs both.

table.name: Open Loop Fueling Floor (Outside Closed Loop)
table.description: Minimum enrichment whenever the engine is out of closed loop for any reason: the mixture is at least this rich. Check it as well as Primary Open Loop Fueling when leaning the open-loop target.

table.name: Open Loop Delay Load Threshold
table.description: Load, by rpm, above which the Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV..., AVCS...) group takes effect after a delay; below it that group is off.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive
table.description: Extra open-loop enrichment added to Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by its DAM multiplier: full at DAM 0, none at DAM 1. Probably the classic knock-dependent extra fuel. Edit with Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive (TGV/AVCS Group).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive DAM Multiplier
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive by the Dynamic Advance Multiplier (DAM), so the extra fuel is added as knock history lowers DAM. Edit with the (TGV/AVCS Group) copy.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive (TGV/AVCS Group)
table.description: Knock-dependent extra enrichment for the TGV/AVCS open-loop group, scaled by its DAM multiplier (full at DAM 0, none at DAM 1).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive DAM Multiplier (TGV/AVCS Group)
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive (TGV/AVCS Group) by DAM (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive (TGV/AVCS Group)
table.description: Fuel removed from the TGV/AVCS open-loop group, scaled by its own DAM multiplier (negative cells add fuel). Leaning only works where Primary Open Loop Fueling is not richer.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier (TGV/AVCS Group)
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive (TGV/AVCS Group) by DAM (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive
table.description: Fuel removed from Primary Open Loop Fueling, scaled by its DAM multiplier (negative cells add fuel). It only leans the target where the TGV/AVCS group is not richer.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier
table.description: Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive by DAM (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Low-DAM Enrichment
table.description: Extra fuel, by rpm and load, that richens the closed-loop target, the closed-loop override and the open-loop floor, scaled up as DAM falls (Low-DAM Enrichment DAM Multiplier). Probably a knock-history safety enrichment.

table.name: Low-DAM Enrichment DAM Multiplier
table.description: Scales Low-DAM Enrichment by DAM.

table.name: Warm-Up Enrichment (TGV Open)
table.description: Coolant-based warm-up enrichment with the TGVs open, blended with Warm-Up Enrichment (TGV Closed) by TGV position and scaled by Warm-Up Enrichment RPM Multiplier. Raising it adds fuel while cold. Warm-up role inferred from the coolant axis.

table.name: Warm-Up Enrichment (TGV Closed)
table.description: Coolant-based warm-up enrichment with the TGVs closed, blended with Warm-Up Enrichment (TGV Open) by TGV position. Raising it adds fuel while cold.

table.name: Warm-Up Enrichment RPM Multiplier
table.description: Scales the warm-up enrichment by rpm (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Warm-Up Enrichment (Coolant Window Override)
table.description: Replaces the warm-up enrichment for a while after start, but only when the start coolant falls inside a calibrated window.

table.name: Fuel Factor Correction (RPM x Load)
table.description: General fuel correction by rpm and load in open and closed loop (128 = no change, each count about 0.4 %). Probably a light-load base-fuel correction.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (Alternate)
table.description: Replacement for Primary Open Loop Fueling plus its knock additive, used only when the calibration switch 'Open Loop Fueling. Edit with Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate) if you enable it.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV/AVCS Group, Alternate)
table.description: Replacement for the TGV/AVCS open-loop group plus its knock additive, used only with the 'Use Alternate Map' calibration switch set.

table.name: Additional Enrichment A
table.description: Extra enrichment added to the open-loop enrichment at higher coolant and lower rpm.

table.name: Additional Enrichment B
table.description: Second table of the additional enrichment, used at low coolant or high rpm.

table.name: Additional Enrichment Throttle Threshold
table.description: Throttle opening above idle, by rpm, needed to enable Additional Enrichment A/B.

table.name: Closed Loop Target (TGVs Open, EGR Off)
table.description: Closed-loop lambda target with the TGVs open and little or no EGR. Picked by TGV state and estimated EGR flow, then limited by the Closed Loop Target Lean Limit tables. Targets richer than lambda 0.80 drop the ECU into open loop (Closed Loop Minimum Target).

table.name: Closed Loop Target (TGVs Closed, EGR Active)
table.description: Closed-loop lambda target with the TGVs closed and EGR flowing. Picked by TGV state and estimated EGR flow, then limited by the Closed Loop Target Lean Limit tables. Targets richer than lambda 0.80 drop the ECU into open loop (Closed Loop Minimum Target).

table.name: Closed Loop Target (TGVs Closed, EGR Off)
table.description: Closed-loop lambda target with the TGVs closed and EGR closed or nearly closed. Picked by TGV state and estimated EGR flow, then limited by the Closed Loop Target Lean Limit tables. Targets richer than lambda 0.80 drop the ECU into open loop (Closed Loop Minimum Target).

table.name: Closed Loop Target (TGVs Open, EGR Active)
table.description: Closed-loop lambda target with the TGVs open and EGR flowing. Picked by TGV state and estimated EGR flow, then limited by the Closed Loop Target Lean Limit tables. Targets richer than lambda 0.80 drop the ECU into open loop (Closed Loop Minimum Target).

table.name: Closed Loop Target Lean Limit (TGVs Closed, Other Modes)
table.description: Caps the closed-loop target at no leaner than this, by coolant and load; values below neutral force a richer target when cold. Used with TGVs closed outside normal combustion mode.

table.name: Closed Loop Target Lean Limit (TGVs Closed, Normal Mode)
table.description: Caps the closed-loop target at no leaner than this, by coolant and load; values below neutral force a richer target when cold. Used with TGVs closed in normal combustion mode.

table.name: Closed Loop Target Lean Limit (TGVs Open, Other Modes)
table.description: Caps the closed-loop target at no leaner than this, by coolant and load; values below neutral force a richer target when cold. Used with TGVs open outside normal combustion mode.

table.name: Closed Loop Target Lean Limit (TGVs Open, Normal Mode)
table.description: Caps the closed-loop target at no leaner than this, by coolant and load; values below neutral force a richer target when cold. Used with TGVs open in normal combustion mode.

table.name: Closed Loop Target Cold-Start Trim (TGVs Open)
table.description: Small trim to the closed-loop target after a cold start, by start coolant and air used since start, with the TGVs not closed.

table.name: Closed Loop Target Cold-Start Trim (TGVs Closed)
table.description: Small trim to the closed-loop target after a cold start, by start coolant and air used since start, with the TGVs closed.

table.name: Closed Loop Target (Catalyst Monitor Active)
table.description: Closed-loop target used instead of the four Closed Loop Target tables while the P0420 catalyst monitor test runs; not limited or trimmed by the other target tables.

table.name: Closed Loop Target Override
table.description: Alternate closed-loop target (plus Low-DAM Enrichment) that replaces the final target under a fuel-routine condition that has not been identified.

table.name: Closed Loop Minimum Target
table.description: Richest target allowed in closed loop: if the target is richer than this, the ECU switches to open loop.

table.name: Closed Loop Integral Gain (Negative Error)
table.description: How fast closed-loop fuel trim corrects when the error is negative, by rpm and load. Larger = faster correction, too large can make the trims oscillate.

table.name: Closed Loop Integral Gain (Positive Error)
table.description: How fast closed-loop fuel trim corrects when the error is positive, by rpm and load. Larger = faster correction, too large can make the trims oscillate.

table.name: Closed Loop Integral Error Shaping (Idle, Negative Error)
table.description: Shapes how the closed-loop error size turns into a trim step (multiplied by Closed Loop Integral Gain). Used with the pedal released and negative error.

table.name: Closed Loop Integral Error Shaping (Idle, Positive Error)
table.description: Shapes how the closed-loop error size turns into a trim step (multiplied by Closed Loop Integral Gain). Used with the pedal released and positive error.

table.name: Closed Loop Integral Error Shaping (Warm, Negative Error)
table.description: Shapes how the closed-loop error size turns into a trim step (multiplied by Closed Loop Integral Gain). Used with the pedal pressed, coolant at or above 50 degC and negative error.

table.name: Closed Loop Integral Error Shaping (Cold, Negative Error)
table.description: Shapes how the closed-loop error size turns into a trim step (multiplied by Closed Loop Integral Gain). Used with the pedal pressed, coolant below 50 degC and negative error.

table.name: Closed Loop Integral Error Shaping (Warm, Positive Error)
table.description: Shapes how the closed-loop error size turns into a trim step (multiplied by Closed Loop Integral Gain). Used with the pedal pressed, coolant at or above 50 degC and positive error.

table.name: Closed Loop Integral Error Shaping (Cold, Positive Error)
table.description: Shapes how the closed-loop error size turns into a trim step (multiplied by Closed Loop Integral Gain). Used with the pedal pressed, coolant below 50 degC and positive error.

table.name: Closed Loop Learning Averaging Passes
table.description: Number of passes the closed-loop correction is averaged over before each long-term trim learning update, by rpm and load; probably the learning window.

table.name: Closed Loop Learning Step
table.description: How much long-term fuel trim changes per learning update, by the size of the averaged closed-loop correction.

table.name: LTFT Coolant Scaling (Positive)
table.description: Scales a learned long-term trim that adds fuel, by coolant (128 = x1.0).

table.name: LTFT Coolant Scaling (Negative)
table.description: Scales a learned long-term trim that removes fuel, by coolant (128 = x1.0).

table.name: LTFT Load Range Boundary 1
table.description: Load boundary 1 of the 10 long-term fuel trim cells (5 load ranges x 2 rpm ranges); load range 1 is below this value.

table.name: LTFT Load Range Boundary 2
table.description: Load boundary 2 of the 10 long-term fuel trim cells (5 load ranges x 2 rpm ranges); load range 2 is below this value.

table.name: LTFT Load Range Boundary 3
table.description: Load boundary 3 of the 10 long-term fuel trim cells (5 load ranges x 2 rpm ranges); load range 3 is below this value.

table.name: LTFT Load Range Boundary 4
table.description: Load boundary 4 of the 10 long-term fuel trim cells (5 load ranges x 2 rpm ranges); load range 4 is below this value.

table.name: LTFT RPM Range Boundary
table.description: Engine speed that splits the long-term fuel trim cells into a low-rpm and a high-rpm set.

table.name: LTFT Floor (Restricted)
table.description: Lowest learned long-term trim allowed under certain conditions (not fully decoded).

table.name: Transient Fuel Throttle-Rate Gain
table.description: Acceleration/deceleration fuel on throttle movement, by coolant: larger = more fuel when the throttle opens and less when it closes. The table the manual car uses, every pass while running. Keep the three Transient Fuel Throttle-Rate Gain tables consistent.

table.name: Transient Fuel Throttle-Rate Gain (AT/CVT)
table.description: AT/CVT version of Transient Fuel Throttle-Rate Gain; only used with an automatic/CVT coding, no effect on a manual car.

table.name: Transient Fuel Throttle-Rate RPM Multiplier
table.description: Scales the throttle-movement transient fuel by rpm (256 = x1.0). Raise it for more tip-in fuel at that rpm. Not active for the first second with the pedal released or at steady idle at standstill.

table.name: Transient Fuel Throttle-Rate Term Minimum
table.description: Largest fuel reduction the throttle-closing side of the transient fuel may command, by coolant.

table.name: Transient Fuel Film Target
table.scaling: mg fuel (film target at gain 1.0) uint16
table.description: Fuel film mass target (mg) by load and rpm; when it rises, the difference is added to the following injections and then decays, compensating fuel film build-up (inferred). The values are fuel mass, but the load axis is fuel-based and scales with Injector Scaling: after changing Injector Scaling, multiply the load axis by new raw / 2918 to keep the same real loads.

table.name: Transient Fuel Film Gain RPM Multiplier
table.description: Scales the load-rise (film) transient fuel by rpm while it adds fuel (128 = x1.0). Companion of Transient Fuel Film Target.

table.name: Transient Fuel Injected-Cylinder Mask (Event Index 0)
Y Axis
table.scaling: injection events since last pass uint8

table.description: Tells the transient fuel logic which cylinders were injected since the last pass, following the firing order 1-3-2-4. Do not edit unless the injection order changes.

table.name: Transient Fuel Injected-Cylinder Mask (Event Index 1)
Y Axis
table.scaling: injection events since last pass uint8

table.description: Tells the transient fuel logic which cylinders were injected since the last pass, following the firing order 1-3-2-4. Do not edit unless the injection order changes.

table.name: Transient Fuel Injected-Cylinder Mask (Event Index 2)
Y Axis
table.scaling: injection events since last pass uint8

table.description: Tells the transient fuel logic which cylinders were injected since the last pass, following the firing order 1-3-2-4. Do not edit unless the injection order changes.

table.name: Transient Fuel Injected-Cylinder Mask (Event Index 3)
Y Axis
table.scaling: injection events since last pass uint8

table.description: Tells the transient fuel logic which cylinders were injected since the last pass, following the firing order 1-3-2-4. Do not edit unless the injection order changes.

table.name: Standstill Tip-In Enrichment
table.description: Extra fuel when pulling away from standstill, by coolant; the largest active enrichment wins. Probably a cold drive-away aid. Triggered below 5 km/h as the pedal is first pressed.

table.name: Standstill Tip-In Enrichment Hold Time
table.description: How long Standstill Tip-In Enrichment is held at full amount before it decays, by coolant.

table.name: Standstill Tip-In Enrichment Decay
table.description: How fast Standstill Tip-In Enrichment fades after the hold time, by coolant; larger = faster fade.

table.name: Fuel Cut Recovery Enrichment (Pedal Pressed)
table.description: Extra fuel after a fuel cut, by cut duration and coolant, while the oxygen sensor still reads lean and the pedal is pressed; probably to restore the catalyst. Longer cuts give more.

table.name: Fuel Cut Recovery Enrichment (Pedal Released)
table.description: Extra fuel after a fuel cut while the sensor still reads lean and the pedal is released; probably to restore the catalyst.

table.name: TGV Transition Enrichment (Closing)
table.description: Short fuel adder after the TGVs start to move, below 3600 rpm and only when cold (TGV Transition Enrichment Coolant Multiplier). Initial amount after a closing event, by rpm and load.

table.name: TGV Transition Enrichment (Closing, Alternate)
table.description: Alternate version of TGV Transition Enrichment (Closing), used under an unidentified condition.

table.name: TGV Transition Enrichment Decay Step (Closing)
table.description: Short fuel adder after the TGVs start to move, below 3600 rpm and only when cold (TGV Transition Enrichment Coolant Multiplier). How fast the closing adder fades after its hold, by rpm.

table.name: TGV Transition Enrichment Decay Step (Closing, Alternate)
table.description: Alternate version of TGV Transition Enrichment Decay Step (Closing), used under an unidentified condition.

table.name: TGV Transition Enrichment Decay Step (Opening)
table.description: How fast the TGV-opening fuel adder fades after its hold.

table.name: TGV Transition Enrichment Decay Step (Opening, Alternate)
table.description: Alternate version of TGV Transition Enrichment Decay Step (Opening), used under an unidentified condition.

table.name: TGV Transition Enrichment Hold Time (Closing)
table.description: Short fuel adder after the TGVs start to move, below 3600 rpm and only when cold (TGV Transition Enrichment Coolant Multiplier). How long the closing adder is held before fading.

table.name: TGV Transition Enrichment Hold Time (Opening)
table.description: How long the TGV-opening fuel adder is held before fading.

table.name: TGV Transition Enrichment Coolant Multiplier
table.description: Scales the TGV transition fuel adders by coolant.

table.name: Event Fuel Adder Initial Hold (A7E2 bit0 Clear)
table.description: Part of a fuel adder triggered when the idle becomes steady with the pedal released, in one fuel mode only. How long the adder is held; AT/CVT-coding table, the manual car uses the Set table.

table.name: Event Fuel Adder Initial Hold (A7E2 bit0 Set)
table.description: Part of a fuel adder triggered when the idle becomes steady with the pedal released, in one fuel mode only. How long the adder is held; the table the manual car uses.

table.name: Event Fuel Adder Decay Step (A7E2 bit0 Clear)
table.description: Part of a fuel adder triggered when the idle becomes steady with the pedal released, in one fuel mode only. How fast the adder fades after the hold; AT/CVT-coding table, the manual car uses the Set table.

table.name: Event Fuel Adder Decay Step (A7E2 bit0 Set)
table.description: Part of a fuel adder triggered when the idle becomes steady with the pedal released, in one fuel mode only. How fast the adder fades after the hold; the table the manual car uses.

table.name: Transient Fuel Throttle-Rate Gain (MT Coding)
table.description: Alternate version of Transient Fuel Throttle-Rate Gain used only when a transmission-coding switch is changed.

table.name: Tip-In Extra Pulse Angle
table.description: Part of an extra fuel pulse on fast tip-in. Probably the injection angle of that extra pulse, by rpm.

table.name: Tip-In Extra Pulse RPM Multiplier
table.description: Part of an extra fuel pulse on fast tip-in. Scales the extra pulse by rpm (128 = x1.0).

table.name: Tip-In Extra Pulse Coolant Multiplier
table.description: Part of an extra fuel pulse on fast tip-in. Scales the extra pulse by coolant (64 = x1.0), out of neutral.

table.name: Tip-In Extra Pulse Coolant Multiplier (Neutral)
table.description: Part of an extra fuel pulse on fast tip-in. Scales the extra pulse by coolant (64 = x1.0) while in neutral.

table.name: Cranking Fuel (First Attempt)
table.description: Main cranking fuel pulse by coolant, for a normal first cranking attempt. Raise for more fuel while cranking. Raw units: change it proportionally.

table.name: Cranking Fuel (Repeat Attempt)
table.description: Cranking fuel pulse by coolant used on a repeat attempt, after a previous attempt already injected fuel and reached 800 rpm or cranked a while. Raw units: change it proportionally.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Coolant Multiplier (Restart after Key-Off)
table.description: Multiplier on the cranking fuel by coolant when restarting after the engine was switched off with the key (start type meaning inferred). Edit with Cranking Fuel Secondary Coolant Multiplier (Restart after Key-Off).

table.name: Cranking Fuel Coolant Multiplier (Restart after Stall)
table.description: Multiplier on the cranking fuel by coolant when restarting after a stall with the ignition still on (start type meaning inferred). Edit with the Secondary copy.

table.name: Cranking Fuel RPM Multiplier (TGV Closed)
table.description: Reduces cranking fuel as cranking rpm rises, by rpm and coolant, TGVs closed side of a TGV blend (255 = x1.0, inferred). Edit the TGV Closed / Open pair together.

table.name: Cranking Fuel RPM Multiplier (TGV Open)
table.description: Reduces cranking fuel as cranking rpm rises, by rpm and coolant, TGVs open side of a TGV blend (255 = x1.0, inferred). Edit the TGV Closed / Open pair together.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Barometric Multiplier
table.description: Cranking fuel multiplier by what is probably barometric pressure, for starting at altitude.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Pedal Multiplier
table.description: Cranking fuel multiplier by accelerator position.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Decay (First Attempt)
table.description: How fast the cranking fuel floor fades away after the engine starts, by start coolant, on a first attempt. 65536 = no decay, smaller = faster fade.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Decay (Repeat Attempt)
table.description: How fast the cranking fuel floor fades after the engine starts, by start coolant, on a repeat attempt. 65536 = no decay, smaller = faster fade.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary (First Attempt)
table.description: Secondary cranking fuel pulse by coolant (first attempt). It is the cranking pulse whenever the engine cranks in normal combustion mode instead of the start mode: after about 10 s of continuous cranking, when the low-rail-pressure start latch is set (then scaled by Cranking Fuel Secondary Low Rail Pressure Multiplier), or on a re-crank before the start sequence reset; it also sets a floor on fuel in normal running until it decays. Raw units: change it proportionally.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary (Repeat Attempt)
table.description: Secondary cranking fuel pulse by coolant (repeat attempt). It is the cranking pulse whenever the engine cranks in normal combustion mode instead of the start mode: after about 10 s of continuous cranking, when the low-rail-pressure start latch is set (then scaled by Cranking Fuel Secondary Low Rail Pressure Multiplier), or on a re-crank before the start sequence reset; it also sets a floor on fuel in normal running until it decays. Raw units: change it proportionally.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary Coolant Multiplier (Restart after Key-Off)
table.description: Secondary-path copy of Cranking Fuel Coolant Multiplier (Restart after Key-Off): multiplier by coolant after a key-off restart.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary Coolant Multiplier (Restart after Stall)
table.description: Secondary-path copy of Cranking Fuel Coolant Multiplier (Restart after Stall): multiplier by coolant after a stall restart.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary Decay (First Attempt)
table.description: How fast the secondary cranking fuel floor fades after the engine starts, by start coolant, on a first attempt (per 10 ms pass). 65536 = no decay, smaller = faster fade. Keep equal to Cranking Fuel Decay (First Attempt).

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary Decay (Repeat Attempt)
table.description: How fast the secondary cranking fuel floor fades after the engine starts, by start coolant, on a repeat attempt (per 10 ms pass). 65536 = no decay, smaller = faster fade. Keep equal to Cranking Fuel Decay (Repeat Attempt).

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary RPM Multiplier (TGV Closed)
table.description: Secondary-path copy of Cranking Fuel RPM Multiplier (TGV Closed): reduces secondary cranking fuel as rpm rises. Edit the TGV Closed / Open pair together.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary RPM Multiplier (TGV Open)
table.description: Secondary-path copy of Cranking Fuel RPM Multiplier (TGV Open): reduces secondary cranking fuel as rpm rises. Edit the TGV Closed / Open pair together.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary Low Rail Pressure Multiplier
table.description: Multiplies the secondary cranking fuel by coolant when rail pressure is still low some time into a start (64 = x1.0).

table.name: Low Rail Pressure Start Enrichment
table.description: Extra fuel by coolant when rail pressure is still low some time into a start, until pressure has stayed close to target for a while.

table.name: Start Enrichment (Load, TGV Open)
table.description: Start-path enrichment by load and coolant with the TGVs open, blended with the TGV Closed table by TGV position. Raising it adds fuel during start-up.

table.name: Start Enrichment (Load, TGV Closed)
table.description: Start-path enrichment by load and coolant with the TGVs closed, blended with the TGV Open table by TGV position and scaled by Start Enrichment (Load) RPM Multiplier.

table.name: Start Enrichment (Load) RPM Multiplier
table.description: Scales Start Enrichment (Load, TGV Closed) by rpm (128 = x1.0); the TGV Open table is not scaled.

table.name: Start Enrichment Additive (Load, TGV Closed)
table.description: Extra start enrichment by load and coolant, added on top of Start Enrichment (Load) only while a start condition flag is set (depends on start coolant, pedal and speed; not fully decoded). TGVs closed side of a TGV blend.

table.name: Start Enrichment Additive (Load, TGV Open)
table.description: Extra start enrichment by load and coolant, added on top of Start Enrichment (Load) only while a start condition flag is set (depends on start coolant, pedal and speed; not fully decoded). TGVs open side of a TGV blend.

table.name: Start Enrichment (Coolant Window Override)
table.description: Replaces Start Enrichment (Load) for a while after start, but only when the start coolant falls inside a calibrated window.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment 1 (Index 0)
table.description: Early-2015 LV9N-software version (LV9N101C / LV9N100F only; LF75404S and later use the TGV-split tables) of After-Start Enrichment 1: after-start enrichment by coolant, one of four tables chosen by a start index (this is index 0), with no TGV split. Faded by After-Start Enrichment Decay 1 (Index 0); numbering matched to the later builds by inference.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment 1 (TGV Open)
table.description: Start-path after-start enrichment by coolant, faded to zero by its decay table; the largest of the three after-start terms is used, scaled by After-Start Enrichment RPM Multiplier. Used with the TGVs open.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment 1 (TGV Closed)
table.description: Start-path after-start enrichment by coolant, faded to zero by its decay table; the largest of the three after-start terms is used, scaled by After-Start Enrichment RPM Multiplier. Used with the TGVs closed.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment Decay 1 (TGV Open)
table.description: Fade time for After-Start Enrichment 1: the enrichment falls linearly to zero over this time after start (unfaded while cranking). Larger = longer enrichment. Used with the TGVs open.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment Decay 1 (TGV Closed)
table.description: Fade time for After-Start Enrichment 1: the enrichment falls linearly to zero over this time after start (unfaded while cranking). Larger = longer enrichment. Used with the TGVs closed.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment 2 (TGV Open)
table.description: Start-path after-start enrichment by coolant, faded to zero by its decay table; the largest of the three after-start terms is used, scaled by After-Start Enrichment RPM Multiplier. Used with the TGVs open.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment 2 (TGV Closed)
table.description: Start-path after-start enrichment by coolant, faded to zero by its decay table; the largest of the three after-start terms is used, scaled by After-Start Enrichment RPM Multiplier. Used with the TGVs closed.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment Decay 2 (TGV Open)
table.description: Fade time for After-Start Enrichment 2: the enrichment falls linearly to zero over this time after start (unfaded while cranking). Larger = longer enrichment. Used with the TGVs open.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment Decay 2 (TGV Closed)
table.description: Fade time for After-Start Enrichment 2: the enrichment falls linearly to zero over this time after start (unfaded while cranking). Larger = longer enrichment. Used with the TGVs closed.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment 3 (TGV Open)
table.description: Start-path after-start enrichment by coolant, faded to zero by its decay table; the largest of the three after-start terms is used, scaled by After-Start Enrichment RPM Multiplier. Used with the TGVs open.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment 3 (TGV Closed)
table.description: Start-path after-start enrichment by coolant, faded to zero by its decay table; the largest of the three after-start terms is used, scaled by After-Start Enrichment RPM Multiplier. Used with the TGVs closed.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment Decay 3 (TGV Open)

table.name: After-Start Enrichment Decay 3 (TGV Closed)
table.description: Fade time for After-Start Enrichment 3: the enrichment falls linearly to zero over this time after start (unfaded while cranking). Larger = longer enrichment. Used with the TGVs closed.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment RPM Multiplier
table.description: Scales the largest of the three after-start enrichments by rpm (128 = x1.0) while cranking and running.

table.name: After-Start Enrichment Coolant Multiplier (Repeat Start)
table.description: Computed after a repeat crank but never used by the fuel calculation, so editing it does nothing.

table.name: Running After-Start Enrichment 1 (First Start)
table.description: Running-path after-start enrichment 1 by coolant for a first start (start type meaning inferred). The ECU uses the largest of the three terms, each faded by its decay table; cut at very high load. Also blocks long-term trim learning while active.

table.name: Running After-Start Enrichment 1 (Restart after Key-Off)

table.name: Injection Timing (Single Injection)
table.description: Main injection angle in normal running (degrees BTDC of compression TDC, larger = earlier), by rpm and load, with one injection per cycle. Replaced by Injection Timing (High Pedal) at high pedal.

table.name: Injection Timing (High Pedal)
table.description: Injection angle used instead of Injection Timing (Single Injection) and its additive while the pedal is at 90 % or more (released below 85 %).

table.name: Injection Timing Additive
table.description: Retard (degrees later) applied to Injection Timing (Single Injection), scaled by Injection Timing Additive Multiplier.

table.name: Injection Timing Additive Multiplier
table.description: Scales Injection Timing Additive (255 = x1.0), by an unidentified input and intake air temperature.

table.name: Cranking Injection Timing
table.description: Injection angle while cranking and for the first 0.3 s of running, by rpm and coolant, but only when the engine is in normal combustion mode (fuel mode 1): after about 10 s of cranking, when the low-rail-pressure start latch is set, or on a re-crank before the start sequence reset. A normal start uses Start Injection Angle (Fuel Mode 0) instead.

table.name: Start Injection Angle (Fuel Mode 0)
table.description: Injection angle in the first phase after start, by rpm and coolant: a compression-stroke injection, probably for the stratified start. Kept within 0.5-180 BTDC.

table.name: Double Injection Quantity Window Low
table.description: Lower fuel-quantity limit for using two injections per cycle; with Double Injection Quantity Window High it defines when split injection is used.

table.name: Double Injection Quantity Window High
table.description: Upper fuel-quantity limit for two injections per cycle.

table.name: Triple Injection Quantity Window Low
table.description: Lower fuel-quantity limit for using three injections per cycle.

table.name: Triple Injection Quantity Window High
table.description: Upper fuel-quantity limit for three injections per cycle.

table.name: Start Injection Angle (Stop-Start Restart, Low Rail Pressure)
table.description:
Injection angle while cranking for a stop-start restart with rail pressure below 2 MPa. Stop-start cannot activate in this calibration, so probably unused. Not clamped by the ECU: keep it within 0.5-180 BTDC. Edit with the High Rail Pressure table.
Details: When used: while cranking (fuel state FFF8906B = 2) with the stop-start restart request FFF89066 bit 0 set and rail pressure FFF88884 below cal 0x2A65E (3279 = 2.0 MPa / 290 psi) (0x0CFB28, called from 0x0C589C with (906B, coolant FFF88A44, rpm/50, cal 0x38448 bit 7, FFF89066 bit 0, FFF88884, &FFF8B050, &FFF8B008), args read in the caller's disassembly). Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the injected cylinder's compression TDC (720 - code/2; larger = earlier), same scale as every injection-angle table (my research notes). It replaces Start Injection Angle (Fuel Mode 0) in FFF8B050, which 0x0CB394 uses as the first-pulse angle of injectors in fuel mode 0 (segment 3, offset B050 - 1080) (read). Unlike that table it is only floored at code 0, not clamped to 1080-1439, so keep it within 180-0.5 BTDC (code 1080-1439) (read). Setting cal 0x38448 bit 7 would force cal 0x11EBC (clamped to 1080-1439) instead. FFF89066 bit 0 = CAN 0x15A byte 2 bit 0, the restart request of the engine stop-start feature (signals_rates_can.md, my research notes, read). Edit with the High Rail Pressure table. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Start Injection Angle (Stop-Start Restart, High Rail Pressure)
table.description:
Injection angle while cranking for a stop-start restart with rail pressure at or above 2 MPa. Probably unused (stop-start cannot activate). Not clamped: keep within 0.5-180 BTDC.
Details: When used: as Start Injection Angle (Stop-Start Restart, Low Rail Pressure), but with rail pressure FFF88884 at or above cal 0x2A65E (3279 = 2.0 MPa / 290 psi) (0x0CFB28, read). Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the injected cylinder's compression TDC (720 - code/2; larger = earlier), same scale as every injection-angle table (my research notes). Only floored at code 0, not clamped (read): keep it within 180-0.5 BTDC (code 1080-1439). FFF89066 bit 0 = CAN 0x15A byte 2 bit 0, the restart request of the engine stop-start feature (signals_rates_can.md, my research notes, read). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Cranking Injection Timing (Stop-Start Restart)
table.description:
Replaces Cranking Injection Timing while cranking for a stop-start restart. Stop-start cannot activate in this calibration, so probably unused.
Details: When used: while cranking (FFF8906B = 2) with the stop-start restart request FFF89066 bit 0 set; then it replaces Cranking Injection Timing as the main injection angle FFF8B052 (0x0CFE8C, read; args read in 0x0C589C: param_5 = coolant FFF88A44, param_11 = FFF89066 bit 0). Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the injected cylinder's compression TDC (720 - code/2; larger = earlier), same scale as every injection-angle table (my research notes). Clamped to code 360-1079 = 180.5-540 BTDC (read). Cal 0x38448 bit 6 would force cal 0x11FE6. FFF89066 bit 0 = CAN 0x15A byte 2 bit 0, the restart request of the engine stop-start feature (signals_rates_can.md, my research notes, read). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Injection Timing (Double Injection, 1st)
table.description: Angle of the first pulse when two injections per cycle are used.

table.name: Injection Timing (Double Injection, 2nd)
table.description: Angle of the second pulse with two injections per cycle.

table.name: Injection Timing (Triple Injection, 1st)
table.description: Angle of the first pulse with three injections per cycle.

table.name: Injection Timing (Triple Injection, 2nd)
table.description: Angle of the second pulse with three injections per cycle.

table.name: Injection Timing (Triple Injection, 3rd)
table.description: Angle of the third pulse with three injections per cycle.

table.name: Double Injection Split
table.description:
Share of the fuel in the first of two injections; the second gets the rest.
Details: Share of the fuel in the first of two injections (0x0D05D8 -> FFF8B068 -> FFF8A6D1, read); the second gets the rest (0x0D0D50). Limited by FFF8A6DA (read). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Triple Injection Split 1
table.description:
Share of the fuel in the first of three injections (the third gets what the first two leave).
Details: Share of the fuel in the first of three injections (0x0D06EC -> FFF8A6C9 -> FFF8A6D3, read); the third gets 128 minus the first two (0x0D0DC0). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Triple Injection Split 2
table.description:
Share of the fuel in the second of three injections.
Details: Share of the fuel in the second of three injections (0x0D06EC -> FFF8A6CA -> FFF8A6D4, read). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Spark Retard
table.description: How far spark is retarded from base timing during cold-start catalyst heating, which heats the catalyst faster. The spark moves toward this target in steps.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Spark Retard (Phase 2)
table.description: Same as Catalyst Heating Spark Retard for the second catalyst-heating phase; its result also selects the phase 2 injection angles.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Injection Angle
table.description: Injection angle during stratified catalyst heating, by rpm and spark target: a compression-stroke pulse that follows the retarded spark (inferred).

table.name: Catalyst Heating Injection Angle 2
table.description: Angle of the second (late, after top dead centre) pulse during stratified catalyst heating, by spark target; negative = after TDC.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Second Injection Share
table.description: Share of fuel moved into the late second pulse during stratified catalyst heating (combustion mode 2). 0 = single injection.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Normal)
table.description: Second-pulse injection angle in catalyst-heating phase 2, by rpm and spark target; compression stroke, limited to 10.5-180 BTDC. Used when the TGVs are not closed.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Normal, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description: AT/CVT version of Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Normal). Only used with the automatic/CVT transmission coding; no effect on a manual car.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Closed)
table.description: Second-pulse injection angle in catalyst-heating phase 2, by rpm and spark target; compression stroke, limited to 10.5-180 BTDC. Used when the TGVs are closed.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Closed, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description: AT/CVT version of Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Closed). Only used with the automatic/CVT transmission coding; no effect on a manual car.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base (TGV Normal)
table.description: First-pulse (intake stroke) injection angle in catalyst-heating phase 2 and the start sequence, by rpm and coolant, limited to 180.5-360 BTDC. Used when the TGVs are not closed.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base (TGV Closed)
table.description: First-pulse (intake stroke) injection angle in catalyst-heating phase 2 and the start sequence, by rpm and coolant, limited to 180.5-360 BTDC. Used when the TGVs are closed.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base Adder (TGV Normal)
table.description: Rpm x load correction to Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base (TGV Normal); positive = later. TGVs not closed.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base Adder (TGV Closed)
table.description: Rpm x load correction to the phase 2 first-pulse angle with the TGVs closed; positive = later.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base Spark Adder (TGV Normal)
table.description: Correction by spark target and coolant to the phase 2 first-pulse angle, TGVs not closed; positive = later.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base Spark Adder (TGV Closed)
table.description: Correction by spark target and coolant to the phase 2 first-pulse angle, TGVs closed; positive = later.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Adder (TGV Normal)
table.description: Correction to Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Normal), the second pulse; positive = later. Edit with that table.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Adder (TGV Closed)
table.description: Correction to the phase 2 second-pulse angle with the TGVs closed; positive = later.

table.name: Start Split Injection Second Share (Idle)
table.description: Share of fuel moved into the second (compression-stroke) pulse during the start / catalyst-heating phase 2, by rpm and coolant (0 = single injection). Used with the pedal released and the car stopped.

table.name: Start Split Injection Second Share
table.description: Share of fuel moved into the second (compression-stroke) pulse during the start / catalyst-heating phase 2, by rpm and coolant (0 = single injection). Used with the pedal pressed or the car moving.

table.name: Start Split Injection Second Share (Idle, Alternate)
table.description: Share of fuel moved into the second (compression-stroke) pulse during the start / catalyst-heating phase 2, by rpm and coolant (0 = single injection).

table.name: Spark Angle Before Running (Coolant)
table.description: Spark value assumed before the engine reaches running mode, used only to choose the catalyst-heating phase 2 injection angles; it is not the actual cranking spark.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Exit Threshold (Neutral Switch On)
table.description: Coolant-based threshold of an internal counter at which catalyst-heating phase 2 ends and normal running starts, used while the neutral switch is on.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Exit Threshold (Neutral Switch Off)
table.description: Coolant-based threshold of an internal counter at which catalyst-heating phase 2 ends and normal running starts, used in gear (neutral switch off).

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Maximum Time
table.description: Longest time catalyst-heating phase 2 may last, by coolant.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Maximum Time
table.description: Longest time the stratified catalyst-heating phase may last.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Coolant Minimum
table.description: Lowest coolant temperature at which stratified catalyst heating is allowed.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Coolant Maximum
table.description: Highest coolant temperature at which stratified catalyst heating is allowed.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Rail Pressure Minimum
table.description: Minimum rail pressure needed for stratified catalyst heating.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Readiness Idle Stability Time
Y Axis
table.scaling: RPM change per combustion event int16

table.description: How long the idle must be steady (pedal released, normal running) before the catalyst-heating readiness flag sets, by rpm change and rpm versus idle target. Its exact role after that is inferred.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Delay
table.description: Delay between the closed-pedal decel fuel cut condition being met and cylinders starting to be cut, by coolant and rpm.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Resume RPM Adder (Coolant)
table.description: Added to the idle target to set the rpm at which the decel fuel cut ends (and, 200 rpm higher, where it starts), by coolant. Raising it probably ends the cut at a higher rpm.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Resume RPM Adder (Low Speed)
table.description: Extra resume-rpm adder for the decel fuel cut below 15 km/h, by coolant. Raising it probably ends the cut at a higher rpm.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Staging Time (Gear 1, A/C Off)
table.description: Decel fuel cut staging for gear 1 (and 0) with the A/C off (inferred): for each rpm band, the times after the cut starts at which 1, 2, 3 and all 4 cylinders are cut. Lower = faster, harsher cut. Values should rise along each row. Manual coding.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Staging Time (Gear 1, A/C On)
table.description: Decel fuel cut staging for gear 1 (and 0) with the A/C engaged (inferred): for each rpm band, the times after the cut starts at which 1, 2, 3 and all 4 cylinders are cut. Lower = faster, harsher cut. Values should rise along each row. Manual coding.

table.description: Decel fuel cut staging for gear 4 with the A/C off (inferred): for each rpm band, the times after the cut starts at which 1, 2, 3 and all 4 cylinders are cut. Lower = faster, harsher cut. Values should rise along each row. Manual coding.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Staging Time (Gear 4, A/C On)
table.description: Decel fuel cut staging for gear 4 with the A/C engaged (inferred): for each rpm band, the times after the cut starts at which 1, 2, 3 and all 4 cylinders are cut. Lower = faster, harsher cut. Values should rise along each row. Manual coding.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Staging Time (Gear 5, A/C Off)
table.description: Decel fuel cut staging for gear 5 with the A/C off (inferred): for each rpm band, the times after the cut starts at which 1, 2, 3 and all 4 cylinders are cut. Lower = faster, harsher cut. Values should rise along each row. Manual coding.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Staging Time (Gear 5, A/C On)
table.description: Decel fuel cut staging for gear 5 with the A/C engaged (inferred): for each rpm band, the times after the cut starts at which 1, 2, 3 and all 4 cylinders are cut. Lower = faster, harsher cut. Values should rise along each row. Manual coding.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Staging Time (Gear 6, A/C Off)
table.description: Decel fuel cut staging for gear 6 (and above) with the A/C off (inferred): for each rpm band, the times after the cut starts at which 1, 2, 3 and all 4 cylinders are cut. Lower = faster, harsher cut. Values should rise along each row. Manual coding.

table.description: Decel fuel cut staging for gear 6 (and above) with the A/C engaged (inferred): for each rpm band, the times after the cut starts at which 1, 2, 3 and all 4 cylinders are cut. Lower = faster, harsher cut. Values should rise along each row. Manual coding.
