table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Resume RPM Adder (A/C, Alternate)
table.description: Alternate A/C resume-rpm adder for the decel fuel cut, by an unidentified CAN-derived value.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Staging Time (Alternate Set, A/C Off)
table.description: Alternate decel fuel cut staging (A/C off).

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Staging Time (Alternate Set, A/C On)
table.description: Alternate decel fuel cut staging (A/C on).

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Full-Cut Shortcut Hold
table.description: Time, by rpm, after which all cylinders would be cut at once under unidentified conditions.

table.name: Purge Rate Limit (Off-Idle)
Y Axis
table.scaling: % fuel removed at 100 % purge rate uint16

table.description: Maximum canister purge rate by learned vapour concentration, scaled by Purge Rate Limit Coolant Multiplier; less purge when the vapour is rich. Used with the pedal pressed.

table.name: Purge Rate Limit (Idle)
Y Axis
table.scaling: % fuel removed at 100 % purge rate uint16

table.description: Maximum canister purge rate by learned vapour concentration, scaled by Purge Rate Limit Coolant Multiplier; less purge when the vapour is rich. Used with the pedal released while an unidentified input bit is set.

table.name: Purge Rate Limit (Idle, Input Bit Clear)
Y Axis
table.scaling: % fuel removed at 100 % purge rate uint16

table.description: Maximum purge rate with the pedal released while an unidentified input bit is clear.

table.name: Purge Rate Limit Coolant Multiplier
table.description: Scales all three Purge Rate Limit tables by coolant (255 = x1.0).

table.name: Purge Rate Limit (Fallback)
table.description: Purge capacity by rpm and load used instead of the vacuum-based capacity when one of several unidentified fault/status flags is set.

table.name: Purge Rate Ramp Step (Off-Idle)
Y Axis
table.scaling: % fuel removed at 100 % purge rate uint16

table.description: How much the purge rate rises per learning update once vapour concentration has been learned, pedal pressed, by learned concentration.

table.name: Purge Rate Ramp Step (Idle)
Y Axis
table.scaling: % fuel removed at 100 % purge rate uint16

table.description: Purge-rate rise per learning update at idle (pedal released) after learning.

table.name: Purge Rate Cut Recovery Step (Off-Idle)
table.scaling: % of purge rate per update uint16
table.description: How fast a purge cut is released, pedal pressed, by how much margin the closed-loop correction has above its lower limit.

table.name: Purge Rate Cut Recovery Step (Idle)
table.scaling: % of purge rate per update uint16
table.description: How fast a purge cut is released at idle (pedal released).

table.name: Purge Rate (Open-Loop Enrichment)
table.description: Purge rate by load while open-loop enrichment is active.

table.name: Purge Air Density (IAT, Baro)
table.description: Air density by intake temperature and barometric pressure, used to compute purge flow capacity. Exact physics: normally no reason to edit.

table.name: Purge Valve Duty
table.description: Purge valve duty needed for a target purge flow at a given manifold vacuum; higher vacuum needs less duty. Applied above Purge Valve Minimum Duty. Change only for a different purge valve.

table.name: Purge Valve Maximum Flow
table.description: Maximum purge flow (air volume, L/s) the valve can pass at a given manifold vacuum; sets the purge capacity. Change only for a different purge valve, together with Purge Valve Duty.

table.name: Purge Valve Minimum Duty
table.description: Duty at which the purge valve starts to flow, by battery voltage and vacuum; the commanded duty is built on top of it.

table.name: Purge Learning Weight (Purge Rate)
table.description: Weight by purge rate on how much each sample moves the learned vapour concentration (255 = x1.0).

table.name: Purge Learning Weight (Purge Flow)
table.description: Weight by purge flow on how much each sample moves the learned vapour concentration (255 = x1.0).

table.name: Purge Learning Weight (Trim Deviation)
table.description: Weight by the size of the closed-loop correction on the vapour concentration learning (255 = x1.0); a dead band so small trim noise does not move it.

table.name: Purge Injector Minimum Pulse Margin
table.description: Margin above Injector Minimum Pulse Width, by rail pressure: when an injector pulse comes this close to the minimum (or the fuel trim nears its lower limit) with rich purge vapour, the ECU cuts purge so fuel can still be metered.

table.name: Base Timing (EGR Off, TGV Open)
table.description: Base (upper-limit) ignition timing map for pedal pressed, EGR off and TGVs open, which covers wide-open throttle and high rpm. The ECU fires the lower of this map and Primary Ignition plus knock correction advance and fine learning.

table.name: Base Timing (EGR Off, TGV Closed)
table.description: Base (upper-limit) ignition timing map used while the pedal is pressed, EGR is off (or only a few percent) and the TGVs are closed (typically cold or light-load running). The ECU fires the lower of this map and Primary Ignition plus knock correction advance and fine learning, so raising cells adds timing only where this map is the lower one.

table.name: Base Timing (EGR Active, TGV Open)
table.description: Base (upper-limit) ignition timing map used while the pedal is pressed, EGR is active and the TGVs are open (part-throttle cruising). The ECU fires the lower of this map and Primary Ignition plus EGR advance, knock correction advance and fine learning, so raising cells adds timing only where this map is the lower one. One of four base maps selected by EGR and TGV state.

table.name: Base Timing (EGR Active, TGV Closed)
table.description: Base (upper-limit) ignition timing map used while the pedal is pressed, EGR is active and the TGVs are closed. The ECU fires the lower of this map and Primary Ignition plus knock correction advance and fine learning (then feedback knock correction and retards apply), so raising cells adds timing only where this map is the lower one. One of four base maps selected by EGR and TGV state; that the switching module is EGR is inferred.

table.name: Minimum Ignition Timing (Coolant)
table.description: Lowest timing the ECU will fire, by coolant temperature, used with the pedal pressed and the throttle between about 3 % and 46 % open; otherwise Minimum Ignition Timing applies. Lowering it allows more retard.

table.name: Minimum Ignition Timing
table.description: Lowest timing the ECU will ever fire when Minimum Ignition Timing (Coolant) does not apply. Final timing is never allowed below this.

table.name: Ignition Dwell Time
table.description: Coil charge (dwell) time in milliseconds by rpm and battery voltage, used whenever the engine runs. More dwell gives a stronger spark but heats the coils.

table.name: Base Timing IAT Compensation
table.description: Timing added (negative = retard) for hot intake air, by intake air temperature, scaled by Base Timing IAT Compensation Multiplier. Applied once the engine is running above about 800 rpm and feeds into base timing.

table.name: Base Timing IAT Compensation 2
table.description: A second timing correction for intake air temperature, only in some software versions: scaled by Base Timing IAT Compensation Multiplier 2 and added to Base Timing IAT Compensation. Where it exists, edit both IAT pairs together.

table.name: Base Timing IAT Compensation Multiplier
table.description: Scales Base Timing IAT Compensation by rpm and load: 0 = no intake-temperature timing correction, 1.0 = the full amount.

table.name: Base Timing IAT Compensation Multiplier 2
table.description: Scales Base Timing IAT Compensation 2 by rpm and load: 0 = no correction from the second curve, 1.0 = the full amount.

table.name: Base Timing Coolant Compensation (TGV Open)
table.description: Timing added to base timing on a cold engine, by coolant temperature, for the TGV-open side; scaled by Base Timing Coolant Compensation Weight (TGV Open) and blended with the TGV Closed table by how far the TGVs are open. Active above about 800 rpm.

table.name: Base Timing Coolant Compensation (TGV Closed)
table.description: Timing added to base timing on a cold engine, by coolant temperature, for the TGV-closed side, blended with the TGV Open table by how far the TGVs are open. Active above about 800 rpm. Keep consistent with Base Timing Coolant Compensation (TGV Open).

table.name: Base Timing Coolant Compensation Weight (TGV Open)
table.description: Percentage (by rpm and load) of Base Timing Coolant Compensation (TGV Open) actually applied. Lower values reduce the cold-engine timing correction in that area.

table.name: Timing Request Enrichment Retard
table.description: Retard ramped into the timing request while open-loop power enrichment is active, by load and rpm. The ECU fires the lower of Base Timing and request + knock advance.

table.name: Base Timing Coolant Compensation (Alternate, Below 5000 RPM)
table.description: Alternate cold-engine timing correction by coolant temperature, used below 5000 rpm only when a calibration switch selects the alternate tables.

table.name: Base Timing Coolant Compensation (Alternate, Above 5000 RPM)
table.description: Alternate cold-engine timing correction by coolant temperature, used above 5000 rpm only when a calibration switch selects the alternate tables.

table.name: Filtered RPM Rate Timing Term
table.description:
Timing added or removed according to how fast engine speed is changing, which looks like an rpm-oscillation (surge) damper.
0x0DB888 (called from 0x0DF0B8 with FFF8AA85 bit 1 and FFF8A8A1 bit 7, read): while FFF8AA85 bit 1 is set (set by 0x07FA1A when the surge damping trigger FFF8A7A1 bit 2 and FFF8A8A2 bit 6 are clear, the request is not being shaped (FFF8AEC2 <= FFF8AEBE), FFF8CEC1 bits 0-4 (rpm and load window flags) are set, speed >= cal 0x57576, gear FFF8A621 within cals 0x57577..0x57578, and FFF886AB bit 7 or FFF8A88F), FFF8A757 = clamp((this(FFF88CA4) + cal 0x2FEDE (s8 -3) x (rpm k passes ago - filtered rpm k passes ago) >> 7) x 100 >> 8, cal 0x2FEDD.. cal 0x2FEDC); k = 05B784/05B790(gear FFF8A621) + 1 (both all 0, so k = 1); rpm history FFF88CAC.. and the filtered-rpm history FFF88CC8.. (FFF8CE9A, a second lag of FFF8CEB2) (read). A757 is added to the base timing sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600, read). Axis: FFF88CA4 = change of the lag-filtered rpm FFF8CEB2 between passes of 0x07E96C (read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Knock Correction Advance Max A (TGV Open)
table.description: First part of the knock correction advance (timing added as DAM rises), by rpm and load, for TGVs open; blended with the TGV Closed table and scaled by KCA DAM Curve A. It is added to the Primary Ignition request, not to the Base Timing map: the ECU fires the lower of Base Timing and Primary + knock advance + fine learning, so raising it adds timing only where that sum is still below Base Timing.

table.name: Knock Correction Advance Max A (TGV Closed)
table.description: First part of the knock correction advance (timing added as DAM rises), by rpm and load, for TGVs closed; blended with the TGV Open table and scaled by KCA DAM Curve A. It is added to the Primary Ignition request, not to the Base Timing map: the ECU fires the lower of Base Timing and Primary + knock advance + fine learning, so raising it adds timing only where that sum is still below Base Timing.

table.name: Knock Correction Advance Max B (TGV Open)
table.description: Second part of the knock correction advance, by rpm and load, for TGVs open. The total available advance is Max A plus Max B; it raises the Primary Ignition side of the timing limit and can never push fired timing above the Base Timing map.

table.name: Knock Correction Advance Max B (TGV Closed)
table.description: Second part of the knock correction advance, by rpm and load, for TGVs closed. Like part A it raises the Primary Ignition side of the timing limit and can never push fired timing above the Base Timing map.

table.name: KCA DAM Curve A
table.description: How much of Knock Correction Advance Max A is applied at each DAM value (0 = none, 1.0 = all). The resulting advance raises the Primary Ignition side of the timing limit, so it reaches the spark only where Primary + advance is below Base Timing.

table.name: KCA DAM Curve B
table.description: How much of Knock Correction Advance Max B is applied at each DAM value. Like part A it acts on the Primary Ignition side of the timing limit, never above Base Timing; keep the axis increasing.

table.name: FBKC Maximum Retard
table.description: Largest amount of timing feedback knock correction can pull. The live knock retard never goes below minus this value, and it applies to all cylinders at once. Raising it allows more protective retard.

table.name: FBKC Retard Step (Knock, State 0x0E)
table.description: Timing pulled by feedback knock correction for each knock event detected above Knock Threshold, in the main knock case. Applied once per combustion event, to all cylinders (there is no per-cylinder knock retard).

table.name: FBKC Retard Step (Knock, State 7)
table.description: Timing pulled by feedback knock correction for each knock event detected above Knock Threshold, in the second main-knock case (an extra internal condition is set). Applied once per combustion event.

table.name: FBKC Recovery Step
table.description: Timing given back by feedback knock correction per combustion event in the non-knock states other than normal knock-free running: when rpm is outside the FBKC window (for example below FBKC Window RPM Minimum), in the closed-pedal / low-load state, and in a few other special states. Inside the window, after knock stops the correction is held for 100 knock-free events and then recovered by FBKC Recovery Step (State 0x0F), not by this value.

table.name: FBKC Recovery Step (State 0x0F)
table.description: Timing given back by feedback knock correction per combustion event after a long knock-free stretch (about 100 events since the last knock). Larger values recover faster.

table.name: FBKC Window RPM Maximum
table.description: Upper rpm limit for feedback knock correction. Above it the current knock retard is held: no new retard and no recovery. Raise this if you raise the rev limit.

table.name: FBKC Window RPM Minimum
table.description: Lower rpm limit for feedback knock correction: below it no new knock retard is taken, and any existing knock retard is given back by FBKC Recovery Step each combustion event.

table.name: DAM Step Gain (FLKC Cell)
FLKC Cell
table.scaling: FLKC cell (5 x rpm range load range) uint8

table.description: How strongly each fine-knock-learning step moves DAM, per FLKC learning cell (index = 5 x rpm range + load range, 0-34; index 0 is the lowest rpm and load cell). Larger values make DAM move faster when the ECU learns knock in that cell; 0 means that cell never moves DAM. Purpose is inferred.

table.name: FLKC Advance Learning Inhibit Zones
Y Axis
table.scaling: zone index (5 x rpm band load band) uint8

table.description: Per rpm/load zone switch: 1 stops fine knock learning from learning timing back upward there, so it can only learn retard (inferred). These zones use their own rpm/load boundaries, not the FLKC cell boundaries.

table.name: FLKC Range Boundary Load 1
table.description: One of the four load boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into load ranges; each learning cell covers one rpm range by one load range. Moving it changes which conditions share a learned correction. Keep them in increasing order.

table.name: FLKC Range Boundary Load 2
table.description: One of the four load boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into load ranges; each learning cell covers one rpm range by one load range. Moving it changes which conditions share a learned correction. Keep them in increasing order.

table.name: FLKC Range Boundary Load 3
table.description: One of the four load boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into load ranges; each learning cell covers one rpm range by one load range. Moving it changes which conditions share a learned correction. Keep them in increasing order.

table.name: FLKC Range Boundary Load 4
table.description: One of the four load boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into load ranges; each learning cell covers one rpm range by one load range. Moving it changes which conditions share a learned correction. Keep them in increasing order.

table.name: FLKC Range Boundary RPM 1
table.description: One of the six rpm boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into rpm ranges. Keep them in increasing order.

table.name: FLKC Range Boundary RPM 2
table.description: One of the six rpm boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into rpm ranges. Keep them in increasing order.

table.name: FLKC Range Boundary RPM 3
table.description: One of the six rpm boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into rpm ranges. Keep them in increasing order.

table.name: FLKC Range Boundary RPM 4
table.description: One of the six rpm boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into rpm ranges. Keep them in increasing order.

table.name: FLKC Range Boundary RPM 5
table.description: One of the six rpm boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into rpm ranges. Keep them in increasing order.

table.name: FLKC Range Boundary RPM 6
table.description: One of the six rpm boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into rpm ranges. Keep them in increasing order.

table.name: FLKC Range Load Hysteresis
table.description: Load hysteresis used when switching between fine learning knock correction load ranges, to stop flicking between cells at a boundary.

table.name: FLKC Range RPM Hysteresis
table.description: Rpm hysteresis used when switching between fine learning knock correction rpm ranges, to stop flicking between cells at a boundary.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend (DAM 0)
table.description: Timing offset added to base timing only at high pedal, blended by DAM with Base Timing DAM Blend (DAM 1); this table applies at DAM 0. 32 = no change, 0.5-degree steps. Not the knock correction advance (renamed from Knock Correction Advance DAM 0/1).

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend (DAM 1)
table.description: Timing offset added to base timing only at high pedal, blended by DAM with Base Timing DAM Blend (DAM 0); this table applies at DAM 1. 32 = no change, 0.5-degree steps. Not the knock correction advance (renamed from Knock Correction Advance DAM 0/1).

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend B (DAM 0)
table.description: Timing offset added to base timing in a high-pedal, enrichment-limited condition in one combustion mode, blended with Base Timing DAM Blend B (DAM 1) by DAM; this table applies at DAM 0. 32 = no change, 0.5-degree steps.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend B (DAM 1)
table.description: Timing offset added to base timing in a high-pedal, enrichment-limited condition in one combustion mode, blended with Base Timing DAM Blend B (DAM 0) by DAM; this table applies at DAM 1. 32 = no change, 0.5-degree steps.

table.name: FBKC Retard Step (Secondary Knock, State 0x0D)
table.description:
Timing pulled per event by feedback knock correction when the secondary knock detector fires.
Details: Feedback knock correction (0x0E2BE4, read): FFF8A79A is an s8 integrator kept at or below 0 and added directly to the fired timing (x 0.3516 degrees, 0x0D9E40): it is the only knock term of that sum, and FFF8A79A is one value for the whole engine, so a knock event on any cylinder retards all four (the fired timing FFF8A744 is recomputed per event for the next cylinder, but no per-cylinder knock retard exists; read). The state FFF8A79C (set once per combustion event by 0x0E2F94 from that event's knock results FFF8A7AD / FFF8A7B5; FFF8A7C1 is the knock-window-length flag (1 = extended window), used there only to reload per-cylinder hold counters FFF84920...FFF84930 from cal 0x27014 when it changes, purpose inferred) picks the action: states 0x0E, 0x0D, 7 and 6 subtract a step (floor = minus FBKC Maximum Retard); states 0x0C, 2, 0 (outside the rpm window) and the other non-knock states (0x0A outside the window, 0x0B) add the recovery step 0x1C271; 0x10 (inside the rpm window, no knock, fewer than cal 0x1C288 = 100 events since the last knock) holds the correction unchanged; 0x0F (inside the window, no knock, >= 100 events) adds 0x1C270, 8/9 add 0x1C272 (capped at 0); 5 = FFF8A79B x 0x1C26E / 128; 3 and 4 load the fixed values 0x1C26F / 0x1C278; 1 = 0. States (0x0E2F94, read, in priority order): 1 = knock control off (cal 0x56EE7 bit 7); 2 = FFF886AB bit 5 or load FFF8ADE4 <= cal 0x1C27E (0); 3 / 4 = FFF88E29 bit 3 / FFF88E2A bit 6 (fixed -14 counts = -4.9 degrees, inferred knock-sensor fault default); 5 = engine speed above FBKC Window RPM Maximum (hold); inside the rpm window: 6 / 0x0D = knock A with / without FFF8AA85 bit 0, 7 / 0x0E = knock B (FFF8A7B5, intensity > Knock Threshold, the active one); 0x0F = no knock and FFF8B130 (events since the last knock, 0x0E7C7C) >= cal 0x1C288 (100), 0x10 = no knock, fewer events; 8 / 9 hold; 0x0A / 0x0B / 0x0C other conditions (0x0B: A/F FFF88AF6 above a lambda threshold). Subtracted per pass in state 0x0D. p16 (read): the FBKC logic 0x0E2F94 (0x0E402C <- 0x07D0E0 <- 0x1E1CBC) is crank-synchronous: one pass per combustion event (180 deg CA, dispatched at tooth position 70 via the ATU-J0 software interrupt 0x0A7390), not per time. Confidence: read.

table.name: FBKC Retard Step (Secondary Knock, State 6)
table.description:
Timing pulled per event by feedback knock correction when the secondary knock detector fires (variant with an extra internal condition set).
Details: Feedback knock correction (0x0E2BE4, read): FFF8A79A is an s8 integrator kept at or below 0 and added directly to the fired timing (x 0.3516 degrees, 0x0D9E40): it is the only knock term of that sum, and FFF8A79A is one value for the whole engine, so a knock event on any cylinder retards all four (the fired timing FFF8A744 is recomputed per event for the next cylinder, but no per-cylinder knock retard exists; read). The state FFF8A79C (set once per combustion event by 0x0E2F94 from that event's knock results FFF8A7AD / FFF8A7B5; FFF8A7C1 is the knock-window-length flag (1 = extended window), used there only to reload per-cylinder hold counters FFF84920...FFF84930 from cal 0x27014 when it changes, purpose inferred) picks the action: states 0x0E, 0x0D, 7 and 6 subtract a step (floor = minus FBKC Maximum Retard); states 0x0C, 2, 0 (outside the rpm window) and the other non-knock states (0x0A outside the window, 0x0B) add the recovery step 0x1C271; 0x10 (inside the rpm window, no knock, fewer than cal 0x1C288 = 100 events since the last knock) holds the correction unchanged; 0x0F (inside the window, no knock, >= 100 events) adds 0x1C270, 8/9 add 0x1C272 (capped at 0); 5 = FFF8A79B x 0x1C26E / 128; 3 and 4 load the fixed values 0x1C26F / 0x1C278; 1 = 0. States (0x0E2F94, read, in priority order): 1 = knock control off (cal 0x56EE7 bit 7); 2 = FFF886AB bit 5 or load FFF8ADE4 <= cal 0x1C27E (0); 3 / 4 = FFF88E29 bit 3 / FFF88E2A bit 6 (fixed -14 counts = -4.9 degrees, inferred knock-sensor fault default); 5 = engine speed above FBKC Window RPM Maximum (hold); inside the rpm window: 6 / 0x0D = knock A with / without FFF8AA85 bit 0, 7 / 0x0E = knock B (FFF8A7B5, intensity > Knock Threshold, the active one); 0x0F = no knock and FFF8B130 (events since the last knock, 0x0E7C7C) >= cal 0x1C288 (100), 0x10 = no knock, fewer events; 8 / 9 hold; 0x0A / 0x0B / 0x0C other conditions (0x0B: A/F FFF88AF6 above a lambda threshold). Subtracted per pass in state 6. p16 (read): the FBKC logic 0x0E2F94 (0x0E402C <- 0x07D0E0 <- 0x1E1CBC) is crank-synchronous: one pass per combustion event (180 deg CA, dispatched at tooth position 70 via the ATU-J0 software interrupt 0x0A7390), not per time. Confidence: read.

table.name: FLKC Counted-Cell Learned Value Threshold
table.description:
By DAM: a fine-knock-learning cell is counted when its learned value is at or above this, and the count sets an internal flag.
0x0E7DF8 (read): one cell per pass, it counts the FLKC cells whose flag FFF811AF[cell] is 1 and whose learned value FFF81414[cell] is at or above this(DAM FFF811AE); after all 35 cells the count goes to FFF8A792 and FFF8A7A3 bit 1 = count >= cal 0x1C699 (4). 0x0E7D0C (read) uses that bit only together with DAM inside cal 0x1C698..0x1C697 (32..48 in DAM x 16 units), which DAM (0..16) never reaches. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (DAM 0)
table.description: Alternate DAM-blended timing offset (DAM 0 side) for base timing. 32 = no change.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (DAM 1)
table.description: Alternate DAM-blended timing offset (DAM 1 side) for base timing. 32 = no change.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 1, Full Window)
table.scaling: knock ratio sum (3 strongest channels) uint16
table.description: Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 1 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the extended (full) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 1 is has not been mapped.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 1, Short Window)
table.scaling: knock ratio sum (3 strongest channels) uint16
table.description: Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 1 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the nominal (short) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 1 is has not been mapped.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 2, Full Window)
table.scaling: knock ratio sum (3 strongest channels) uint16
table.description: Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 2 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the extended (full) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 2 is has not been mapped.

table.description: Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 2 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the nominal (short) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 2 is has not been mapped.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 3, Full Window)
table.scaling: knock ratio sum (3 strongest channels) uint16
table.description: Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 3 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the extended (full) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 3 is has not been mapped.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 3, Short Window)
table.scaling: knock ratio sum (3 strongest channels) uint16
table.description: Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 3 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the nominal (short) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 3 is has not been mapped.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 4, Full Window)
table.scaling: knock ratio sum (3 strongest channels) uint16
table.description: Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 4 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the extended (full) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 4 is has not been mapped.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 4, Short Window)
table.scaling: knock ratio sum (3 strongest channels) uint16
table.description: Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 4 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the nominal (short) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 4 is has not been mapped.

table.name: Secondary Knock Threshold (Event 1)
table.scaling: knock ratio sum (3 strongest channels) uint16
table.description: Second knock detector level by rpm for event slot 1; a signal above it triggers the secondary knock retard steps. Unit: sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background (3.0 = all at background).

table.name: Secondary Knock Threshold (Event 2)
table.scaling: knock ratio sum (3 strongest channels) uint16
table.description: Second knock detector level by rpm for event slot 2; a signal above it triggers the secondary knock retard steps. Unit: sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background (3.0 = all at background).

table.name: Secondary Knock Threshold (Event 3)
table.scaling: knock ratio sum (3 strongest channels) uint16
table.description: Second knock detector level by rpm for event slot 3; a signal above it triggers the secondary knock retard steps. Unit: sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background (3.0 = all at background).

table.name: Secondary Knock Threshold (Event 4)
table.scaling: knock ratio sum (3 strongest channels) uint16
table.description: Second knock detector level by rpm for event slot 4; a signal above it triggers the secondary knock retard steps. Unit: sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background (3.0 = all at background).

table.name: Knock Window Start
table.description: Crank angle (probably degrees after top dead centre) at which the ECU starts listening for knock, by rpm; limited by Knock Window Start Minimum and Maximum.

table.name: Knock Window Length
table.description: Normal length of the knock listening window in crank degrees, by rpm; Knock Window Length Extension may be added at low timing.

table.name: Knock Window Overlap Margin (Event 1)
table.description: For knock event slot 1, by rpm: how many degrees the knock window may run past the next event angle before the ECU flags an overlap, which changes how the knock signal background is adapted. Which cylinder slot 1 is has not been mapped.

table.name: Knock Window Overlap Margin (Event 2)
table.description: For knock event slot 2, by rpm: how many degrees the knock window may run past the next event angle before the ECU flags an overlap, which changes how the knock signal background is adapted. Which cylinder slot 2 is has not been mapped.

table.name: Knock Window Overlap Margin (Event 3)
table.description: For knock event slot 3, by rpm: how many degrees the knock window may run past the next event angle before the ECU flags an overlap, which changes how the knock signal background is adapted. Which cylinder slot 3 is has not been mapped.

table.name: Knock Window Overlap Margin (Event 4)
table.description: For knock event slot 4, by rpm: how many degrees the knock window may run past the next event angle before the ECU flags an overlap, which changes how the knock signal background is adapted. Which cylinder slot 4 is has not been mapped.

table.name: Knock Window Start Minimum
table.description: Lower limit on Knock Window Start.

table.name: Knock Window Start Maximum
table.description: Upper limit on Knock Window Start.

table.name: Knock Window Length Minimum
table.description: Lower limit on the knock window length actually used, with or without the length extension.

table.name: Knock Window Length Maximum
table.description: Upper limit on the knock window length actually used, with or without the length extension.

table.name: Knock Window Length Extension
table.description: Extra crank degrees added to Knock Window Length while timing is at or below Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold, as long as the longer window still ends before the next event. Switching to this longer window also switches the Knock Threshold set (Full Window).

table.name: Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold
table.description: The longer knock window (Knock Window Length Extension) is only allowed while ignition timing is at or below this, i.e. when timing is heavily retarded. It is kept until timing rises above this plus Knock Window Extension Timing Hysteresis.

table.name: Knock Window Extension Timing Hysteresis
table.description: Hysteresis for Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold: once the longer window is in use, timing must rise this far above the threshold before it switches back.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 1, Channel 2)
table.description:
This software version: the table is the step only on the pass where the window flag sets. On the pass where it clears, the longer version subtracts the table; this one adds the fixed value instead (s16; the row for the event is Knock Background Clear Step (Event 1)).
Knock signal processing for event slot 1, channel 2 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock. Larger = that event less likely to count as knock. Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.

table.name: Knock Background Clear Step (Event 1)
table.description: Only in software versions with the shorter knock background function: a fixed value per knock channel added to the knock background on the knock window where the window flag clears (event slot 1). Signal processing; leave alone.

table.name: Knock Background Clear Step (Event 2)
table.description: Only in software versions with the shorter knock background function: a fixed value per knock channel added to the knock background on the knock window where the window flag clears (event slot 2). Signal processing; leave alone.

table.name: Knock Background Clear Step (Event 3)
table.description: Only in software versions with the shorter knock background function: a fixed value per knock channel added to the knock background on the knock window where the window flag clears (event slot 3). Signal processing; leave alone.

table.name: Knock Background Clear Step (Event 4)
table.description: Only in software versions with the shorter knock background function: a fixed value per knock channel added to the knock background on the knock window where the window flag clears (event slot 4). Signal processing; leave alone.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 1, Channel 3)
table.description:
This software version: the table is the step only on the pass where the window flag sets. On the pass where it clears, the longer version subtracts the table; this one adds the fixed value instead (s16; the row for the event is Knock Background Clear Step (Event 1)).
Knock signal processing for event slot 1, channel 3 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.

table.name: Timing Retard High Load (1st Gear)
table.description: Timing pulled at high load in 1st gear (by rpm and load), used only above about 2800 rpm and 0.84 g/rev (65 % load) and not in neutral. Raising values adds retard. Not used if knock control is switched off.

table.name: Timing Retard High Load (2nd Gear)
table.description: Timing pulled at high load in 2nd gear (by rpm and load), used only above about 2800 rpm and 0.84 g/rev (65 % load) and not in neutral. Raising values adds retard. Not used if knock control is switched off.

table.name: Timing Retard High Load (3rd Gear / Fault)
table.description: Timing pulled at high load in 3rd gear (by rpm and load), used above about 2800 rpm and 0.84 g/rev (65 % load) and not in neutral. Also used for every gear, rpm and load when CAN communication or vehicle speed faults are present. Not used if knock control is switched off.

table.name: Timing Retard High Load (4th Gear)
table.description: Timing pulled at high load in 4th gear (by rpm and load), used only above about 2800 rpm and 0.84 g/rev (65 % load) and not in neutral. Raising values adds retard. Not used if knock control is switched off.

table.name: Timing Retard High Load (5th Gear)
table.description: Timing pulled at high load in 5th gear (by rpm and load), used only above about 2800 rpm and 0.84 g/rev (65 % load) and not in neutral. Raising values adds retard. Not used if knock control is switched off.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Start (Below 200 km/h)
table.description: Delay, in 10 ms steps after a sudden throttle opening (tip-in), before the tip-in timing retard starts, by rpm; used below 200 km/h.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Start (From 200 km/h)
table.description: Delay, in 10 ms steps after a sudden throttle opening (tip-in), before the tip-in timing retard starts, by rpm; used at 200 km/h and above.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Decay (Below 200 km/h)
table.description: How fast the tip-in timing retard is removed once its window ends, in degrees per combustion event by rpm; used below 200 km/h. Larger values give timing back faster.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Decay (From 200 km/h)
table.description: How fast the tip-in timing retard is removed once its window ends, in degrees per combustion event by rpm; used at 200 km/h and above. Larger values give timing back faster.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard End (Below 200 km/h)
table.description: How long the tip-in timing retard lasts after a sudden throttle opening, in 10 ms steps by rpm; used below 200 km/h between about 3900 and 6375 rpm.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard End (From 200 km/h)
table.description: How long the tip-in timing retard lasts after a sudden throttle opening, in 10 ms steps by rpm; used from 200 to 250 km/h, between about 3900 and 6375 rpm.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Temperature Adder
table.description: Extra tip-in timing retard added by intake air temperature (from what is probably the second intake air temperature sensor).

table.name: Tip-In Retard Class 4 Start Throttle Maximum
table.description: Tip-in classification by rpm: for the strongest tip-in class (4), the throttle before the stab must be below this. Together with Tip-In Retard Class 4 Throttle Minimum it defines a big low-to-high throttle jump.

table.name: Tip-In Retard Class 4 Throttle Minimum
table.description: Tip-in classification by rpm: for the strongest tip-in class (4), the throttle after the stab must be at or above this.

table.name: Tip-In Retard Class Hold Throttle
table.description: Tip-in classification by rpm: once the pedal has been pressed for a short while and throttle is at or above this, the tip-in class is held rather than reassigned to classes 2/3 or dropped back to 1.

table.name: Tip-Out Timing Retard
table.description: Timing pulled, by gear and manifold pressure, when rpm rises shortly after lifting off the pedal on a warm engine above walking speed; probably damps driveline shunt or coasting downshift jolts. Latched on the event and removed at once afterwards.

table.name: Timing Request Recovery Rate After Tip-Out
table.description: Limits how fast the timing request may climb back to the closed-pedal target just after the pedal is released, by rpm. Lower values give a softer return.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Resume Timing Retard
table.description: Short timing retard by coolant temperature, applied for a few combustion events when fuel comes back after decel fuel cut because rpm fell to the resume point with the pedal still closed; then ramped out. Softens the fuel-return bump. 128 = no change.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Recovery Timing Ramp (Closed-Pedal Resume)
table.description: How fast, in degrees per combustion event by rpm, the -5 degree decel-fuel-cut timing offset is removed after the cut ends with the pedal still released.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Recovery Timing Ramp (Pedal Resume)
table.description: How fast, in degrees per combustion event by rpm, the -5 degree decel-fuel-cut timing offset is removed after the cut ends because the pedal was pressed.

table.name: A/C Cut Timing Retard Hold (RPM)
table.description: When the A/C compressor switches off near standstill, the ECU retards timing 5 degrees for this many combustion events (one per 180 degrees of crank rotation), by rpm, then ramps the retard out. Probably smooths the idle load change.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Curve (Gear 1)
table.description: Manual transmission, gear 1: timing correction (negative = retard) by the size of the throttle-flow change after a throttle step, scaled by the surge phase, coolant and mode factors. Appears to damp driveline surge (shuffle) by retarding while rpm swings up.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Curve (Gear 2)
table.description: Manual transmission, gear 2: timing correction (negative = retard) by the size of the throttle-flow change after a throttle step, scaled by the surge phase, coolant and mode factors. Appears to damp driveline surge (shuffle) by retarding while rpm swings up.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Curve (Gear 3)
table.description: Manual transmission, gear 3: timing correction (negative = retard) by the size of the throttle-flow change after a throttle step, scaled by the surge phase, coolant and mode factors. Appears to damp driveline surge (shuffle) by retarding while rpm swings up.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Curve (Gear 4)
table.description: Manual transmission, gear 4: timing correction (negative = retard) by the size of the throttle-flow change after a throttle step, scaled by the surge phase, coolant and mode factors. Appears to damp driveline surge (shuffle) by retarding while rpm swings up.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Curve (Gear 5)

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Curve (Gear 6)
table.description: Manual transmission, gear 6: timing correction (negative = retard) by the size of the throttle-flow change after a throttle step, scaled by the surge phase, coolant and mode factors. Appears to damp driveline surge (shuffle) by retarding while rpm swings up.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Curve (AT/CVT Gear 1)
table.description: AT/CVT version of Surge Damping Timing Curve (Gear 1).

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Curve (AT/CVT Gear 2)

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Phase Factor (Gear 1, Below 1800 RPM)
table.description: Manual transmission, gear 1, below 1800 rpm: how much of the surge damping timing correction is applied at each step of the rpm swing count (0 = none, 1.0 = full). Appears to target the rpm-rising part of a driveline surge.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Phase Factor (Gear 1, From 1800 RPM)
table.description: Manual transmission, gear 1, from 1800 rpm up: how much of the surge damping timing correction is applied at each step of the rpm swing count (0 = none, 1.0 = full). Appears to target the rpm-rising part of a driveline surge.

table.description: Manual transmission, gear 2, below 1800 rpm: how much of the surge damping timing correction is applied at each step of the rpm swing count (0 = none, 1.0 = full). Appears to target the rpm-rising part of a driveline surge.

table.description: Manual transmission, gear 2, from 1800 rpm up: how much of the surge damping timing correction is applied at each step of the rpm swing count (0 = none, 1.0 = full). Appears to target the rpm-rising part of a driveline surge.

table.description: Manual transmission, gear 3, below 1800 rpm: how much of the surge damping timing correction is applied at each step of the rpm swing count (0 = none, 1.0 = full). Appears to target the rpm-rising part of a driveline surge.

table.description: Manual transmission, gear 3, from 1800 rpm up: how much of the surge damping timing correction is applied at each step of the rpm swing count (0 = none, 1.0 = full). Appears to target the rpm-rising part of a driveline surge.

table.description: Manual transmission, gear 4, below 1800 rpm: how much of the surge damping timing correction is applied at each step of the rpm swing count (0 = none, 1.0 = full). Appears to target the rpm-rising part of a driveline surge.

table.description: Manual transmission, gear 4, from 1800 rpm up: how much of the surge damping timing correction is applied at each step of the rpm swing count (0 = none, 1.0 = full). Appears to target the rpm-rising part of a driveline surge.

table.description: Manual transmission, gear 5, below 1800 rpm: how much of the surge damping timing correction is applied at each step of the rpm swing count (0 = none, 1.0 = full). Appears to target the rpm-rising part of a driveline surge.

table.description: Manual transmission, gear 5, from 1800 rpm up: how much of the surge damping timing correction is applied at each step of the rpm swing count (0 = none, 1.0 = full). Appears to target the rpm-rising part of a driveline surge.

table.description: Manual transmission, 6th gear, from 1800 rpm up: how much of the surge damping timing correction is applied at each step of the rpm swing count.

table.description: AT/CVT version of the surge damping phase factor for gear 1.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Phase Factor (AT/CVT Gear 2)
table.description: AT/CVT version of the surge damping phase factor for gear 2.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Phase Factor (AT/CVT Gear 3)
table.description: AT/CVT version of the surge damping phase factor for gear 3.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Phase Factor (AT/CVT Gear 4)
table.description: AT/CVT version of the surge damping phase factor for gear 4.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Phase Factor (AT/CVT Gear 5)
table.description: AT/CVT version of the surge damping phase factor for gear 5.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Phase Factor (AT/CVT Gear 6)
table.description: AT/CVT version of the surge damping phase factor for gear 6.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Combustion Mode Factor
table.description: Scales the surge damping timing correction by combustion mode (0 = off, 1.0 = full).

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Coolant Factor
table.description: Scales the surge damping timing correction by coolant temperature on this manual-transmission car.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Coolant Factor (AT/CVT)
table.description: AT/CVT version of Surge Damping Timing Coolant Factor.

table.name: Surge Damping Throttle Flow Map
table.description: Converts throttle opening and rpm into a flow fraction (probably how much the throttle limits airflow); how fast this value changes is what triggers and sizes the surge damping timing retard. Changing it changes how strongly a throttle step triggers surge damping.

table.name: A/C Cut Timing Retard Step (Alternate Logic)
table.description: Alternate A/C-switch timing retard amount, by an unidentified input.

table.name: Torque Reduction Spark Retard
table.description: Turns a torque or efficiency shortfall back into spark retard on base timing. Besides torque reduction, it is how the ECU pulls fired timing down to Primary Ignition (or the closed-pedal target) plus knock correction advance where that is below Base Timing, so it must stay the inverse of Ignition Efficiency vs Retard; don't edit one without the other. Not used in the rev/overboost-cut states.

table.name: Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Open)
table.description: Base ignition timing map for the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration) with the TGVs open; from 1200 rpm up its rows equal Base Timing (EGR Off, TGV Open). It is only an upper limit: the ECU fires the lower of this map and Closed-Pedal Timing Target (plus its corrections).

table.name: Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Closed)
table.description: Base ignition timing map for the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration) with the TGVs closed. It is only an upper limit: the ECU fires the lower of this map and Closed-Pedal Timing Target (plus its corrections).

table.name: Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Closed)
table.description: Maximum timing allowed with the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration), by rpm and load, TGV-closed side; blended with Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Open) by how far the TGVs are open. Never limits timing with the pedal pressed. The rpm axis ends at 4,000 rpm.

table.name: Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Open)
table.description: Maximum timing allowed with the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration), by rpm and load, TGV-open side; blended with Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Closed) by how far the TGVs are open. Never limits timing with the pedal pressed.

table.name: Closed-Pedal Timing Target
table.description: Ignition timing target by rpm with the pedal released (idle and coasting) on this manual car; coolant, intake-air and post-start corrections are added. The ECU fires the lower of this and the Pedal Released Base Timing map; it is also fired directly during a scan-tool timing check.

table.name: Closed-Pedal Timing Target (AT Drive Range)
table.description: AT version of Closed-Pedal Timing Target, used with the pedal released while the transmission is probably in a drive range.

table.name: Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation
table.description: Timing added with the pedal released on a cold engine, by coolant temperature, scaled by Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation RPM Multiplier. Adds to the pedal-released base timing and the closed-pedal target.

table.name: Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation RPM Multiplier
table.description: Scales Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation by rpm (1.0 = full amount).

table.name: Post-Start Closed-Pedal Timing Advance (Coolant at Start)
table.description: Extra closed-pedal timing for the first moments after a start (stationary, pedal released, low rpm), by the coolant temperature at start, then ramped out. It raises the closed-pedal timing target. Not applied below about -3 C start coolant.

table.name: Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1)
table.description: Base spark target by rpm and coolant for the cold-start / catalyst-heating mode (pedal released, car stopped, below 4000 rpm); the manual-car set. Torque, run-time and re-entry adders go on top. It feeds the torque model and cold-start monitors; the fired spark probably follows other paths.

table.name: Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1, AT/CVT)
table.description: AT/CVT copy of Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1).

table.name: Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1, AT/CVT, Warm-Up Fallback)
table.description: AT/CVT warm-up fallback copy of Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1).

table.name: Start Spark Target Torque Adder (Mode 1)
table.description: Added to Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1) by torque request (as a fraction of full-load torque) and coolant, in the cold-start / catalyst-heating mode; manual-car set.

table.name: Start Spark Target Run-Time Adder (Mode 1)
table.description: Added to Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1) by time since the engine started running and coolant, in the cold-start / catalyst-heating mode; manual-car set.

table.name: Start Spark Target Run-Time Adder (Mode 1, AT/CVT)
table.description: AT/CVT copy of Start Spark Target Run-Time Adder (Mode 1).

table.name: Start Spark Target Run-Time Adder (Mode 1, AT/CVT, Warm-Up Fallback)
table.description: AT/CVT warm-up fallback copy of Start Spark Target Run-Time Adder (Mode 1).

table.name: Start Spark Target Re-Entry Adder (Mode 1)
table.description: Added to Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1) by time since the engine dropped back from normal running into the cold-start / catalyst-heating mode, and coolant; manual-car set. Zero until the first such re-entry after power-up.

table.name: Start Spark Target Re-Entry Adder (Mode 1, AT/CVT)
table.description: AT/CVT copy of Start Spark Target Re-Entry Adder (Mode 1).

table.name: Start Spark Signal Upper Threshold (Baro)
table.description: Upper threshold, by barometric pressure, on an unidentified signal in the start spark logic: while the signal stays at or above it for a set number of passes, Start Spark Offset Step (Baro) moves the start spark offset. Only in some software versions. Raw units; leave alone.

table.name: Start Spark Signal Lower Threshold (Baro)
table.description: Lower threshold, by barometric pressure, on the same unidentified signal as Start Spark Signal Upper Threshold (Baro): while the signal stays at or below it for a set number of passes, the start spark offset moves the other way. Only in some software versions. Raw units; leave alone.

table.name: Start Spark Offset Step (Baro)
table.description: Step, by barometric pressure, added to the start spark offset on each pass while the start spark signal is outside its thresholds. Only in some software versions. Raw units; leave alone.

table.name: Start Spark Target Re-Entry Adder (Mode 1, AT/CVT, Warm-Up Fallback)
table.description: AT/CVT warm-up fallback copy of Start Spark Target Re-Entry Adder (Mode 1).

table.name: Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1, Warm-Up Fallback)
table.description: Warm-up fallback copy of Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1) for the manual car.

table.name: Start Spark Target Torque Adder (Mode 1, Warm-Up Fallback)
table.description: Warm-up fallback copy of Start Spark Target Torque Adder (Mode 1) for the manual car.

table.name: Start Spark Target Run-Time Adder (Mode 1, Warm-Up Fallback)
table.description: Warm-up fallback copy of Start Spark Target Run-Time Adder (Mode 1) for the manual car.

table.name: Start Spark Target Re-Entry Adder (Mode 1, Warm-Up Fallback)
table.description: Warm-up fallback copy of Start Spark Target Re-Entry Adder (Mode 1) for the manual car.

table.name: Target Boost
table.description: Boost target in absolute pressure, by rpm and the ECU's target torque (the driver's request after the torque limits). Corrected for barometric pressure and intake temperature, then the wastegate control chases it. Raise with Boost Limit.

table.name: Boost Limit
table.description: Boost ceiling by rpm that the torque/throttle model uses as its full-load manifold pressure: the model's target MAP is (torque request / full-load reference torque) x this, and it also scales the throttle-area input. It is not an overboost cut (see Overboost Limit). Raise it together with Target Boost so the model's full-load pressure matches the boost you run.

table.name: Wastegate Duty Initial
table.description: Base (feed-forward) wastegate duty by rpm and target torque, before boost feedback is added. Higher duty = more boost. It is scaled by the wastegate duty baro and IAT compensations and the total is capped by Wastegate Duty Maximum. Faults force 0 % duty.

table.name: Wastegate Duty Maximum
table.description: Ceiling on wastegate duty (Initial plus feedback) by rpm and target torque, scaled by the same baro and IAT compensations. Also stops the boost integral from growing once duty reaches it. Raise it if feedback runs out of authority.

table.name: Target Boost IAT Compensation
table.description: Multiplier on Target Boost and Boost Limit by intake air temperature (1.0 = no change).

table.name: Target Boost Baro Compensation
table.description: Multiplier on Target Boost (and Boost Limit) by rpm and barometric pressure (1.0 = no change).

table.name: Wastegate Duty IAT Compensation
table.description: Multiplier on Wastegate Duty Initial and Maximum by intake air temperature (1.0 = no change).

table.name: Wastegate Duty Baro Compensation
table.description: Multiplier on Wastegate Duty Initial and Maximum by rpm and barometric pressure (1.0 = no change). Edit together with Wastegate Duty IAT Compensation, which it is combined with.

table.name: Boost Proportional
table.description: Proportional wastegate duty added by boost error (target minus actual; positive = under target), scaled by Boost Proportional IAT Gain. Larger values react harder to error. Zero while boost feedback is inactive.

table.name: Boost Integral Step (Positive Error)
table.description: How fast the boost integral adds duty when boost is under target, by boost error; added every 20 ms, scaled by Boost Integral Positive IAT Gain. Only grows above Boost Integral Positive Error Deadband and while duty is below Wastegate Duty Maximum; capped by Boost Integral Maximum.

table.name: Boost Integral Step (Negative Error)
table.description: How fast the boost integral removes duty when boost is over target, by boost error; applied every 20 ms while duty is at least 5 %, scaled by Boost Integral Negative IAT Gain. Floored at Boost Integral Minimum.

table.name: Boost Proportional IAT Gain
table.description: Multiplier on Boost Proportional by intake air temperature (1.0 = no change).

table.name: Boost Integral Negative IAT Gain
table.description: Multiplier on Boost Integral Step (Negative Error) by intake air temperature (1.0 = no change).

table.name: Boost Integral Positive IAT Gain
table.description: Multiplier on Boost Integral Step (Positive Error) by intake air temperature (1.0 = no change).

table.name: Boost Integral Maximum
table.description: Most wastegate duty the boost integral can add.

table.name: Boost Integral Minimum
table.description: Most wastegate duty the boost integral can remove.

table.name: Boost Integral Positive Error Deadband
table.description: The boost integral only adds duty while boost is under target by at least this much, to avoid creeping on tiny errors.

table.name: Boost Feedback Activation Threshold
table.description: Boost feedback (proportional and integral) only runs while the boost target is above atmospheric by more than this, by rpm; otherwise feedback is zero and the integral is reset.

table.name: Boost Feedback Minimum RPM
table.description: Boost feedback (proportional and integral) only runs above this rpm.

table.name: Low-DAM Boost Cut Arming Count
table.description: Cells, counted in one pass over the fine-learning knock cells, with learned correction below the Cell Threshold. Reaching this arms the cut for the next pass. Above 34 it can never arm.

table.name: Low-DAM Boost Cut Cell Threshold
table.description: Learned FLKC below this counts toward arming.

table.name: Low-DAM Boost Cut DAM Threshold
table.description: While armed, DAM below this cuts boost: wastegate duty goes to 0%. 0 disables the cut.

table.name: Low-DAM Boost Cut DAM Release
table.description: Once cut, boost stays cut while DAM is below this.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default)
table.description: Drive mode 1: the default set (used when no SI-Drive request is received; the only set on cars without SI-Drive). Main driver demand map for drive mode 1 (the default and fallback): torque requested from rpm and pedal; sets how much torque (and so throttle and boost) a given pedal gives. Edit together with Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, Monitor) or expect a throttle plausibility fault.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, Monitor)
table.description: Safety-monitor copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default), probably read by the electronic throttle torque monitor. Keep it identical to the main table: change both together or expect a throttle/torque plausibility fault.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport)
table.description: Drive mode 2: SI-Drive Sport (S). Main driver demand map for drive mode 2: torque requested from rpm and pedal; sets how much torque (and so throttle and boost) a given pedal gives. Edit together with Requested Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport, Monitor) or expect a throttle plausibility fault.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport, Monitor)
table.description: Safety-monitor copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport), probably read by the electronic throttle torque monitor. Keep it identical to the main table: change both together or expect a throttle/torque plausibility fault.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent)
table.description: Drive mode 3: SI-Drive Intelligent (I). Main driver demand map for drive mode 3: torque requested from rpm and pedal; sets how much torque (and so throttle and boost) a given pedal gives. Edit together with Requested Torque (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent, Monitor) or expect a throttle plausibility fault.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent, Monitor)
table.description: Safety-monitor copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent), probably read by the electronic throttle torque monitor. Keep it identical to the main table: change both together or expect a throttle/torque plausibility fault.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp)
table.description: Drive mode 4: SI-Drive Sport Sharp (S#). Main driver demand map for drive mode 4: torque requested from rpm and pedal. Edit together with Requested Torque (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp, Monitor) or expect a throttle plausibility fault.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp, Monitor)
table.description: Safety-monitor copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp), probably read by the electronic throttle torque monitor. Keep it identical to the main table: change both together or expect a throttle/torque plausibility fault.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT)
table.description: Drive mode 1: the default set (used when no SI-Drive request is received; the only set on cars without SI-Drive). On the AT/CVT coding this is the whole requested-torque map for this drive mode (Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default) is then ignored); unused on manual cars. Edit it, and its Monitor copy, when tuning an AT/CVT car.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT, Monitor)
table.description: Monitor copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT): keep identical to it or expect a throttle plausibility fault. Used only on the AT/CVT coding.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport, AT/CVT)
table.description: Drive mode 2: SI-Drive Sport (S). On the AT/CVT coding this is the whole requested-torque map for this drive mode (Requested Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport) is then ignored); unused on manual cars. Edit it, and its Monitor copy, when tuning an AT/CVT car.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport, AT/CVT, Monitor)
table.description: Monitor copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport, AT/CVT): keep identical to it or expect a throttle plausibility fault. Used only on the AT/CVT coding.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent, AT/CVT)
table.description: Drive mode 3: SI-Drive Intelligent (I). On the AT/CVT coding this is the whole requested-torque map for this drive mode (Requested Torque (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent) is then ignored); unused on manual cars. Edit it, and its Monitor copy, when tuning an AT/CVT car.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent, AT/CVT, Monitor)
table.description: Monitor copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent, AT/CVT): keep identical to it or expect a throttle plausibility fault. Used only on the AT/CVT coding.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp, AT/CVT)
table.description: Drive mode 4: SI-Drive Sport Sharp (S#). On the AT/CVT coding this is the whole requested-torque map for this drive mode (Requested Torque (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp) is then ignored); unused on manual cars. Edit it, and its Monitor copy, when tuning an AT/CVT car.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp, AT/CVT, Monitor)
table.description: Monitor copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp, AT/CVT): keep identical to it or expect a throttle plausibility fault. Used only on the AT/CVT coding.

table.name: Accelerator Pedal Scaling
table.description: Shapes the accelerator pedal position before it goes into the Requested Torque maps (role inferred). Editing this also changes the second pedal channel, which reads the same data.

table.name: Accelerator Pedal Span
table.description: Pedal sensor voltage travel that counts as 100 % pedal. Normally leave alone; change only for a different pedal sensor.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default)
table.description: Tip-in smoothing for drive mode 1 (the default and fallback mode): how fast the target torque may rise per 10 ms in the first, slow stage of a tip-in, by gear and rpm (scaled by gear and by Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier). Raise for sharper throttle response, lower for smoother.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 2, Sport)
table.description: Tip-in smoothing for drive mode 2: how fast the target torque may rise per 10 ms in the first, slow stage of a tip-in, by gear and rpm (scaled by gear and by Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier). Raise for sharper throttle response, lower for smoother.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent)
table.description: Tip-in smoothing for drive mode 3: how fast the target torque may rise per 10 ms in the first, slow stage of a tip-in, by gear and rpm (scaled by gear and by Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier). Raise for sharper throttle response, lower for smoother.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp)
table.description: Tip-in smoothing for drive mode 4: how fast the target torque may rise per 10 ms in the first, slow stage of a tip-in, by gear and rpm (scaled by gear and by Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier). Raise for sharper throttle response, lower for smoother.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description: AT/CVT version of Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default). Only used on an AT/CVT-coded car, so it has no effect on a manual.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 2, Sport, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description: AT/CVT version of Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 2, Sport). Only used on an AT/CVT-coded car, so it has no effect on a manual.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description: AT/CVT version of Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent). Only used on an AT/CVT-coded car, so it has no effect on a manual.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description: AT/CVT version of Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp). Only used on an AT/CVT-coded car, so it has no effect on a manual.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 (Drive Mode 1, Default)
table.description: Tip-in smoothing for drive mode 1 (default): how fast target torque may rise per 10 ms once past Target Torque Rise Stage 2 Torque, by gear and rpm (scaled by gear and the Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier). Raise for quicker torque build-up.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 (Drive Mode 2, Sport)
table.description: Tip-in smoothing for drive mode 2: how fast the target torque may rise per 10 ms once it is past Target Torque Rise Stage 2 Torque, by gear and rpm (scaled by gear and by the Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier). Raise for quicker torque build-up.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent)
table.description: Tip-in smoothing for drive mode 3: how fast the target torque may rise per 10 ms once it is past Target Torque Rise Stage 2 Torque, by gear and rpm (scaled by gear and by the Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier). Raise for quicker torque build-up.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp)
table.description: Tip-in smoothing for drive mode 4: how fast the target torque may rise per 10 ms once it is past Target Torque Rise Stage 2 Torque, by gear and rpm (scaled by gear and by the Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier). Raise for quicker torque build-up.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description: AT/CVT version of Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 (Drive Mode 1, Default). Only used on an AT/CVT-coded car, so it has no effect on a manual.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 (Drive Mode 2, Sport, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description: AT/CVT version of Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 (Drive Mode 2, Sport). Only used on an AT/CVT-coded car, so it has no effect on a manual.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description: AT/CVT version of Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent). Only used on an AT/CVT-coded car, so it has no effect on a manual.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description: AT/CVT version of Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp). Only used on an AT/CVT-coded car, so it has no effect on a manual.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier
table.description: Multiplies the Stage 1 tip-in rise rate by pedal position, so harder tip-ins build torque faster. Applies to all drive modes.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier
table.description: Multiplies the Stage 2 tip-in rise rate by pedal position, so harder tip-ins build torque faster. Applies to all drive modes.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Stage 2 Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default)
table.description: Tip-in smoothing for drive mode 1 (the default and fallback mode): the torque, by gear and rpm, at which the slow Stage 1 rise hands over to the faster Stage 2 rise. Lower it to reach the fast stage sooner.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Stage 2 Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport)
table.description: Tip-in smoothing for drive mode 2: the torque, by gear and rpm, at which the slow Stage 1 rise hands over to the faster Stage 2 rise. Lower it to reach the fast stage sooner.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Stage 2 Torque (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent)
table.description: Tip-in smoothing for drive mode 3: the torque, by gear and rpm, at which the slow Stage 1 rise hands over to the faster Stage 2 rise. Lower it to reach the fast stage sooner.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Stage 2 Torque (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp)
table.description: Tip-in smoothing for drive mode 4: the torque, by gear and rpm, at which the slow Stage 1 rise hands over to the faster Stage 2 rise. Lower it to reach the fast stage sooner.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Start Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default)
table.description: Tip-in smoothing for drive mode 1 (the default and fallback mode): below this torque (by gear and rpm) the driver's request passes unsmoothed, and the Stage 1 slow rise starts from here.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Start Torque (Drive Mode 2, Sport)
table.description: Tip-in smoothing for drive mode 2: below this torque (by gear and rpm) the driver's request passes unsmoothed, and the Stage 1 slow rise starts from here.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Start Torque (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent)
table.description: Tip-in smoothing for drive mode 3: below this torque (by gear and rpm) the driver's request passes unsmoothed, and the Stage 1 slow rise starts from here.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Start Torque (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp)
table.description: Tip-in smoothing for drive mode 4: below this torque (by gear and rpm) the driver's request passes unsmoothed, and the Stage 1 slow rise starts from here.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Ceiling (Normal)
table.description: Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is the Ceiling, by gear and rpm, for the normal set: the smoothing only acts when the request is below it.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Ceiling (Alternate)
table.description: Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is the Ceiling for the alternate set (chosen by an unidentified flag): smoothing only acts below it.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Threshold (Normal)
table.description: Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is the Threshold, by gear and rpm, for the normal set: where the fast fall (Step A) switches to the slow fall (Step B).

table.name: Target Torque Fall Threshold (Alternate)
table.description: Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is the Threshold, by gear and rpm, for the alternate set (chosen by an unidentified flag): where the fast fall (Step A) switches to the slow fall (Step B).

table.name: Target Torque Fall Threshold (Low Speed)
table.description: Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is the Threshold for the set used below about 4 km/h. In 1st gear it is 74 ft-lb (100 Nm) up to 3600 rpm and 37 ft-lb (50 Nm) above, and the 1st-gear low-speed steps are unlimited, so 1st gear gets practically no smoothing below 4 km/h.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Step A (Normal)
table.description: Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is Step A, the fast fall rate per 10 ms, for the normal set. Raise for quicker tip-out, lower for smoother.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Step A (Alternate)
table.description: Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is Step A, the fast fall rate per 10 ms, for the alternate set (chosen by an unidentified flag). Raise for quicker tip-out, lower for smoother.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Step A (Low Speed)
table.description: Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is Step A, the fast fall rate per 10 ms, for the set used below about 4 km/h. Raise for quicker tip-out, lower for smoother.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Step B (Normal)
table.description: Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is Step B, the slow fall rate per 10 ms below the Threshold, for the normal set.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Step B (Alternate)
table.description: Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is Step B, the slow fall rate per 10 ms below the Threshold, for the alternate set (chosen by an unidentified flag).

table.name: Target Torque Fall Step B (Low Speed)
table.description: Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is Step B, the slow fall rate per 10 ms below the Threshold, for the set used below about 4 km/h.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Ceiling (Low Speed)
table.description: Tip-out smoothing: when the torque request drops, the target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms down to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is the Ceiling for the low-speed set (below about 4 km/h), used in place of Target Torque Fall Ceiling (Normal): the smoothing only acts when the request is below it.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Path B Coolant Rise
table.description: Part of the condition that lets Path B tip-in smoothing act, based on how much the coolant has warmed since start.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Path B Low-Speed Time
table.description: Part of the condition that lets Path B tip-in smoothing act: probably the time the car has been stopped. Its axis input is not identified (raw).

table.name: Target Torque Rise Path B Pedal-Released Low-Speed Time
table.description: Part of the condition that lets Path B tip-in smoothing act: probably the time stopped with the pedal released. Its axis input is not identified (raw).

table.name: Target Torque Rise Stage 2 Torque (Path B, Drive Mode 1, Default)
table.description: Path B tip-in smoothing for drive mode 1 (the default and fallback mode): the torque where Path B's slow stage hands over to its fast stage.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Stage 2 Torque (Path B, Drive Mode 2, Sport)
table.description: Path B tip-in smoothing for drive mode 2: the torque where Path B's slow stage hands over to its fast stage.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Stage 2 Torque (Path B, Drive Mode 3, Intelligent)
table.description: Path B tip-in smoothing for drive mode 3: the torque where Path B's slow stage hands over to its fast stage.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Stage 2 Torque (Path B, Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp)
table.description: Path B tip-in smoothing for drive mode 4: the torque where Path B's slow stage hands over to its fast stage.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Start Torque (Path B, Drive Mode 1, Default)
table.description: Path B tip-in smoothing for drive mode 1 (the default and fallback mode): requests below this pass unsmoothed and Path B's slow stage starts here.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Start Torque (Path B, Drive Mode 2, Sport)
table.description: Path B tip-in smoothing for drive mode 2: requests below this pass unsmoothed and Path B's slow stage starts here.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Start Torque (Path B, Drive Mode 3, Intelligent)
table.description: Path B tip-in smoothing for drive mode 3: requests below this pass unsmoothed and Path B's slow stage starts here.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Start Torque (Path B, Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp)
table.description: Path B tip-in smoothing for drive mode 4: requests below this pass unsmoothed and Path B's slow stage starts here.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Path B, Drive Mode 1, Default)
table.description: Path B tip-in smoothing for drive mode 1 (the default and fallback mode) with manual coding: allowed torque rise per 10 ms in Path B's slow stage.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Path B, Drive Mode 2, Sport)
table.description: Path B tip-in smoothing for drive mode 2 with manual coding: allowed torque rise per 10 ms in Path B's slow stage.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Path B, Drive Mode 3, Intelligent)
table.description: Path B tip-in smoothing for drive mode 3 with manual coding: allowed torque rise per 10 ms in Path B's slow stage.
