table.description: Upper limit on the final exhaust cam target, interpolated by (probably) oil temperature between the Low / Mid / High ceiling tables.

table.name: AVCS Barometric Blend
table.description: Share (0-100 %) of the altitude (A) cam target tables versus the sea-level (B) tables, by barometric pressure.

table.name: High Pedal Entry Threshold
table.description: Accelerator position, by barometric pressure, at or above which the ECU switches to the high-pedal cam targets (set 2), provided vehicle speed is steady. Lowering it uses the high-pedal cams earlier. Other functions also read this high-pedal flag.

table.name: High Pedal Exit Threshold
table.description: Accelerator position below which the high-pedal flag clears and the cams return to the normal (set 1) targets. Keep it below High Pedal Entry Threshold.

table.name: High Pedal Tip-In Rate Threshold
table.description: Pedal-rise rate, by pedal position, that sets the high-pedal flag immediately on a fast stab at the pedal (above about 90 %), for both the high-pedal cam targets and Injection Timing (High Pedal), without waiting for the normal entry delay.

table.name: Intake AVCS Minimum RPM (Oil Temp)
table.description: Minimum engine speed for intake cam control by oil temperature. Below it the cams are held at rest and ignition fades to the AVCS Inactive timing tables.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Minimum RPM (Oil Temp)
table.description: Minimum engine speed for exhaust cam control by oil temperature; works like Intake AVCS Minimum RPM (Oil Temp).

table.name: AVCS Activation Delay After Start
table.description: How long after every start the cams are held at their rest position before cam control begins, by coolant temperature at start. Raise for a longer hold, lower to start cam control sooner.

table.name: AVCS Minimum Oil Temp (IAT at Start)
table.description: Minimum oil temperature before cam control is allowed, by intake air temperature at start (a proxy for how cold the engine was). Below it the cams stay at rest.

table.name: Intake AVCS Fixed Duty Window After Start
table.description: Appears to set how long after a start (by coolant at start) the intake cam valves are held at a fixed 52 % duty instead of closed-loop control. Only matters if longer than AVCS Activation Delay After Start.

table.name: Intake AVCS Fixed Duty Minimum Oil Temp (IAT at Start)
table.description: Appears to set the oil temperature, by intake air temperature at start, above which the intake cam valves are held at a fixed 52 % duty during Intake AVCS Fixed Duty Window After Start instead of closed-loop control. Only acts during Intake AVCS Fixed Duty Window After Start.

table.name: Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Idle, Cam 1)
table.description: Proportional part of the intake cam 1 oil control valve duty by rpm and cam error, used with the pedal fully released and the car below about 4 km/h; otherwise Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 1) is used.

table.name: Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Idle, Cam 2)
table.description: Proportional part of the intake cam 2 oil control valve duty by rpm and cam error, used with the pedal fully released and the car below about 4 km/h; otherwise Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 2) is used.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Feedback Duty (Idle, Cam 1)
table.description: Proportional part of the exhaust cam 1 oil control valve duty by rpm and cam error, used at idle with the pedal fully released; otherwise Exhaust AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 1) is used. Larger values correct cam error faster.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Feedback Duty (Idle, Cam 2)
table.description: Proportional part of the exhaust cam 2 oil control valve duty by rpm and cam error, used at idle with the pedal fully released; otherwise Exhaust AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 2) is used.

table.name: Intake AVCS Rate Feedback Duty (Cam 1)
table.description: Damping (derivative) part of the intake cam 1 oil control valve duty by rpm and how fast the cam error is changing, added to the proportional term during active cam control.

table.name: Intake AVCS Rate Feedback Duty (Cam 2)
table.description: Damping (derivative) part of the intake cam 2 oil control valve duty by rpm and how fast the cam error is changing, added to the proportional term during active cam control.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Rate Feedback Duty (Cam 1)
table.description: Damping (derivative) part of the exhaust cam 1 oil control valve duty by rpm and how fast the cam error is changing; added to the proportional term during active cam control. More damping reduces overshoot.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Rate Feedback Duty (Cam 2)
table.description: Damping (derivative) part of the exhaust cam 2 oil control valve duty by rpm and how fast the cam error is changing; added to the proportional term during active cam control.

table.name: Intake AVCS Rate Feedback Oil Factor
table.description: Oil-temperature multiplier (128 = 1.0) on the intake cam damping term for both cams.

table.name: Intake AVCS Feedback Oil Factor (Normal, Positive Error)
table.description: Oil-temperature multiplier (128 = 1.0) on the driving intake cam proportional duty when the cam lags its target. Applies to both intake cams.

table.name: Intake AVCS Feedback Oil Factor (Normal, Negative Error)
table.description: Oil-temperature multiplier (128 = 1.0) on the driving intake cam proportional duty when the cam is ahead of its target. Applies to both intake cams.

table.name: Intake AVCS Feedback Oil Factor (Idle, Positive Error)
table.description: Oil-temperature multiplier (128 = 1.0) on the idle intake cam proportional duty when the cam lags its target. Applies to both intake cams.

table.name: Intake AVCS Feedback Oil Factor (Idle, Negative Error)
table.description: Oil-temperature multiplier (128 = 1.0) on the idle intake cam proportional duty when the cam is ahead of its target. Applies to both intake cams.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Feedback Oil Factor (Normal, Positive Error)
table.description: Oil-temperature multiplier (128 = 1.0) on the driving exhaust cam proportional duty when the cam lags its target. Applies to both exhaust cams.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Feedback Oil Factor (Normal, Negative Error)
table.description: Oil-temperature multiplier (128 = 1.0) on the driving exhaust cam proportional duty when the cam is ahead of its target. Applies to both exhaust cams.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Feedback Oil Factor (Idle, Positive Error)
table.description: Oil-temperature multiplier (128 = 1.0) on the idle exhaust cam proportional duty when the cam lags its target. Applies to both exhaust cams.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Feedback Oil Factor (Idle, Negative Error)
table.description: Oil-temperature multiplier (128 = 1.0) on the idle exhaust cam proportional duty when the cam is ahead of its target. Applies to both exhaust cams.

table.name: Intake AVCS OCV Battery Voltage Compensation
table.description: Multiplier on both intake oil control valve outputs by battery voltage, so the valves get the same effective drive as voltage changes. Always used.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS OCV Battery Voltage Compensation
table.description: Multiplier on both exhaust oil control valve outputs by battery voltage, so the valves get the same effective drive as voltage changes. Always used.

table.name: Intake AVCS OCV Expected Current
table.description: Expected intake oil control valve current for a given duty; the ECU compares the measured current with it to learn a correction factor.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS OCV Expected Current
table.description: Expected exhaust oil control valve current for a given duty; the ECU compares measured current against it to learn a correction. Same role as Intake AVCS OCV Expected Current.

table.name: Intake AVCS OCV Coil Factor (Oil Temp)
table.description: Multiplier by oil temperature on the intake oil control valve duty, used only for the first moments of cam control after power-up; afterwards the Settled table is used. Probably compensates the valve coil warming with the oil. Edit together with the Settled table.

table.name: Intake AVCS OCV Coil Factor (Oil Temp, Settled)
table.description: Multiplier by oil temperature on the intake oil control valve duty for normal running once cam control has been active a while.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS OCV Coil Factor (Oil Temp)
table.description: Multiplier by oil temperature on the exhaust oil control valve duty, used only briefly before the first active cam-control pass; afterwards the Settled table is used. Edit together with the Settled table.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS OCV Coil Factor (Oil Temp, Settled)
table.description: Multiplier by oil temperature on the exhaust oil control valve duty, used for normal running once cam control has been active.

table.name: Intake AVCS OCV Adaptation Step (Cam 1)
table.description: Step size, by valve current error, for learning the intake cam 1 oil control valve current correction (limited to 0.5-1.5). Larger steps learn faster but can hunt. Used while valve duty is at least 20 %.

table.name: Intake AVCS OCV Adaptation Step (Cam 2)
table.description: Step size, by valve current error, for learning the intake cam 2 oil control valve current correction. Same role as the cam 1 table.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS OCV Adaptation Step (Cam 1)
table.description: Step size, by valve current error, for learning the exhaust cam 1 oil control valve current correction. Same role as the intake tables.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS OCV Adaptation Step (Cam 2)
table.description: Step size, by valve current error, for learning the exhaust cam 2 oil control valve current correction. Same role as the intake tables.

table.name: Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 1)
table.description: Proportional part of the intake cam 1 oil control valve duty by rpm and cam error (target minus actual) while driving (pedal applied or moving). Larger values move the cam faster but can overshoot.

table.name: Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 2)
table.description: Proportional part of the intake cam 2 oil control valve duty by rpm and cam error (target minus actual) while driving (pedal applied or moving). Larger values move the cam faster but can overshoot.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 1)
table.description: Proportional part of the exhaust cam 1 oil control valve duty by rpm and cam error (target minus actual) while driving. Larger values move the cam towards its target faster but can overshoot. The idle variant is used with the pedal released at standstill.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 2)
table.description: Proportional part of the exhaust cam 2 oil control valve duty by rpm and cam error (target minus actual) while driving. Larger values move the cam towards its target faster but can overshoot. The idle variant is used with the pedal released at standstill.

table.name: AVCS Activation Delay After Start (Second)
table.description: A second start-delay table that can only shorten the AVCS hold after the hold has already ended, so it never changes anything. Edit AVCS Activation Delay After Start instead.

table.name: Intake AVCS OCV Current Integral Step
table.description:
Integral step for the intake oil control valve current loop. a calibration setting forces the integral term to zero.
Details: When used: cal 0x3BBD1 = 90 (non-zero) forces the I term to 0 (0x15ED58, read). Otherwise the I term FFF868EC (limits +/-25 by cal 0x3BBC6/0x3BBC8, then 0...2) moves by this(current error) x cal 0x3BBBC/100 / 32768 per pass and is added before the battery factor. Read by 0x15ED58 (cam 1) and as 05E71C by 0x15F158 (cam 2), same data 0x03BC50. 0x15ED58 / 0x15F158 (intake cam 1 / 2) and 0x163394 / 0x163788 (exhaust cam 1 / 2), read: OCV output = (I term + duty FFF8B8EA x coil factor x adaptation factor) x battery factor, stored x25 into FFF8B8EE (intake cam 1). The adaptation factor (0.5...1.5, cal 0x3BBCE/0x3BBCC) is stepped by the current error = expected current (Expected Current table) - measured FFF88D70 x 2.5/65536 while the duty is >= 20 % (cal 0x3BBC4). Confidence: read.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS OCV Current Integral Step
table.description:
Integral step for the exhaust oil control valve current loop. a calibration setting forces the exhaust integral term to zero.
Details: When used: cal 0x3CACD = 90 forces the exhaust I term to 0 (0x163394, read). Same role as Intake AVCS OCV Current Integral Step; read as 05EA4C by 0x163788 (same data 0x03CB4C). Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake OCV Base Duty (Cam 1, Legacy Path)
table.description:
Base intake cam 1 valve duty by rpm for an older, byte-based cam control path.
Base term by rpm of the intake cam 1 OCV duty in the legacy byte-based AVCS path: about 49.2-52.0 % duty before the FFF88AA4 factor; the learned and feedback bytes are added around 128 (= 51.2 %). Module (read): seg 0x100000 0x104xxx-0x106xxx is the byte-based cam path; 0x10466C (intake, called at seg_0x100000.c:3516 with rpm CD54, FFF88AA4, learned bytes FFF8147A/147C/147E, feedback bytes FFF8B368, cam errors B956/B954) forms per cam: B352 = this(rpm) x 026EB0/026EC0(FFF88AA4)/128; B356 = 147A if the cam error >= cal 0x26E82 (364 = 2.0 deg), 147C if <= cal 0x26E84 (-2.0 deg), else 128; B366 = clamp(B368 + B352 + 147E + B356 - 384, 0, 250). 0x106A0C does the same for the exhaust cams (05CF08/05CF14, factors 0298F4/029904, errors B916/B914, thresholds cal 0x298C6/0x298C8) into B380. The OCV duty routines 0x15DF20 / 0x15E63C (intake cam 1 / 2) and 0x16269C / 0x162D18 (exhaust) set duty B8DE = B366[cam] x 10 (B380 for exhaust) only when cal 0x3CCC4 bit 0 is clear (read). FFF88AA4 = (FFF88AE6 >> 8 - 10) x 1.6 (0x060000 area, read); FFF88AE6 not identified. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Intake OCV Base Duty (Cam 2, Legacy Path)
table.description:

Base term by rpm of the intake cam 2 OCV duty in the legacy byte-based AVCS path: about 48.8-50.8 % duty before the FFF88AA4 factor; the learned and feedback bytes are added around 128 (= 51.2 %). The OCV duty routines 0x15DF20 / 0x15E63C (intake cam 1 / 2) and 0x16269C / 0x162D18 (exhaust) set duty B8DE = B366[cam] x 10 (B380 for exhaust) only when cal 0x3CCC4 bit 0 is clear (read). FFF88AA4 = (FFF88AE6 >> 8 - 10) x 1.6 (0x060000 area, read); FFF88AE6 not identified. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Exhaust OCV Base Duty (Cam 1, Legacy Path)

Base term by rpm of the exhaust cam 1 OCV duty in the legacy byte-based AVCS path: about 48.8-50 % duty before the FFF88AA4 factor; the learned and feedback bytes are added around 128 (= 51.2 %). Module (read): seg 0x100000 0x104xxx-0x106xxx is the byte-based cam path; 0x10466C (intake, called at seg_0x100000.c:3516 with rpm CD54, FFF88AA4, learned bytes FFF8147A/147C/147E, feedback bytes FFF8B368, cam errors B956/B954) forms per cam: B352 = this(rpm) x 026EB0/026EC0(FFF88AA4)/128; B356 = 147A if the cam error >= cal 0x26E82 (364 = 2.0 deg), 147C if <= cal 0x26E84 (-2.0 deg), else 128; B366 = clamp(B368 + B352 + 147E + B356 - 384, 0, 250). 0x106A0C does the same for the exhaust cams (05CF08/05CF14, factors 0298F4/029904, errors B916/B914, thresholds cal 0x298C6/0x298C8) into B380. FFF88AA4 = (FFF88AE6 >> 8 - 10) x 1.6 (0x060000 area, read); FFF88AE6 not identified. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Exhaust OCV Base Duty (Cam 2, Legacy Path)
table.description:
Base exhaust cam 2 valve duty by rpm for an older, byte-based cam control path.
Base term by rpm of the exhaust cam 2 OCV duty in the legacy byte-based AVCS path: about 47.2-50.8 % duty before the FFF88AA4 factor; the learned and feedback bytes are added around 128 (= 51.2 %). Module (read): seg 0x100000 0x104xxx-0x106xxx is the byte-based cam path; 0x10466C (intake, called at seg_0x100000.c:3516 with rpm CD54, FFF88AA4, learned bytes FFF8147A/147C/147E, feedback bytes FFF8B368, cam errors B956/B954) forms per cam: B352 = this(rpm) x 026EB0/026EC0(FFF88AA4)/128; B356 = 147A if the cam error >= cal 0x26E82 (364 = 2.0 deg), 147C if <= cal 0x26E84 (-2.0 deg), else 128; B366 = clamp(B368 + B352 + 147E + B356 - 384, 0, 250). 0x106A0C does the same for the exhaust cams (05CF08/05CF14, factors 0298F4/029904, errors B916/B914, thresholds cal 0x298C6/0x298C8) into B380. table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, Mode 5)
table.description: Main idle speed target by coolant in normal running; this is the table to edit to change idle speed on a manual car. Automatic/CVT cars use Mode 6 instead.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, AT/CVT, Mode 6)
table.description: Warm idle speed target by coolant for automatic/CVT cars only; a manual car never uses this table.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Post-Start, Modes 1/2)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant right after a start (below 75 degC coolant) until the car moves or the engine warms to 50 degC, and while the engine is stopped. Raise for a higher fast-idle after cold starts.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm Start, Mode 3)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant after a hot restart (coolant at or above 75 degC at start), until the car moves. Raise for a higher idle right after hot starts.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, Mode 7)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant once the car has driven off after a cold start but the engine is still warming up (until coolant is above about 75 degC); then idle returns to Mode 5. Used on manual cars.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, AT/CVT, Mode 8)
table.description: Automatic/CVT version of Idle Speed Target (Warm-Up Drive-Off, Mode 7): idle speed by coolant once the car has moved off before the engine is warm. Never used on a manual car.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (In Drive, AT/CVT)
table.description: Idle speed target by coolant while an automatic/CVT car idles in Drive with the brake on (pedal released, slow). Never used on a manual car (inferred).

table.name: Idle Speed Minimum (Baro, Oil Temp)
table.description: Floor on the idle speed target by barometric pressure and oil temperature; the ECU idles at no less than this.

table.name: Idle Post-Start Mode Exit Coolant
table.description: Coolant temperature, by coolant at start, at which idle leaves the post-start mode for normal warm idle (it also leaves once the car moves).

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 1 to 2)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 2 (cold post-start). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 1 to 3)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 3 (warm-start). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 1 to 5)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 5 (warm idle). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 2 to 5)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 2 (cold post-start) to mode 5 (warm idle). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 2 to 7)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 2 (cold post-start) to mode 7 (warm-up drive-off). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 3 to 5)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 3 (warm-start) to mode 5 (warm idle). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 3 to 7)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 3 (warm-start) to mode 7 (warm-up drive-off). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 7 to 5)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 7 (warm-up drive-off) to mode 5 (warm idle). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 1 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 2 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 2 (cold post-start) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 2 to 8)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 2 (cold post-start) to mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 3 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 3 (warm-start) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 3 to 8)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 3 (warm-start) to mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 4 to 6)
table.description:
How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 4 (cold idle) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Coolant FFF88A44 axis. Mode 1 -> 1 uses step 0. This table: mode 4 -> 6. Modes 6/8 only occur with the AT/CVT coding: 0x0F2BCC passes A7F6 through when FFF88ADA bit7 is set and 0x0F354C itself only yields 1-5/7, so this step is never used by this MT calibration; it also needs idle mode 4. p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 5 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 5 (warm idle) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 6 to 4)
table.description:
How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle) to mode 4 (cold idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Coolant FFF88A44 axis. Mode 1 -> 1 uses step 0. This table: mode 6 -> 4. Modes 6/8 only occur with the AT/CVT coding: 0x0F2BCC passes A7F6 through when FFF88ADA bit7 is set and 0x0F354C itself only yields 1-5/7, so this step is never used by this MT calibration; it also needs idle mode 4. p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 6 to 5)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle) to mode 5 (warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 7 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 7 (warm-up drive-off) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 7 to 8)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 7 (warm-up drive-off) to mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 8 to 5)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off) to mode 5 (warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 8 to 6)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 8 to 7)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 8 (AT/CVT warm-up drive-off) to mode 7 (warm-up drive-off). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Cold Idle, Mode 4)
table.description:
Idle speed target by coolant for a cold-idle mode used when stopped below a coolant threshold.
Details: When used: idle mode 4, entered from mode 5 when stopped with coolant below cal 0x24E94 for cal 0x24E96 passes. 0x0F1BCC selects this boot-format table by idle mode FFF8A7F0 = 4 and coolant; the result B238 is ramped (0x0F1D00) and becomes the idle target FFF8B236 through the minimum-speed max() in 0x0F2274 (read). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Fallback Latch)
table.description:
Idle target ramp rate (by coolant) used when a warm-up fallback flag is set (manual-car version).
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Used instead of the mode table when FFF899D7 bit0 rises while the idle mode is unchanged (index 98/99, 0x0F1DD0, read). FFF899D7 bit0 is the warm-up fallback latch. This one when FFF8A7E2 bit0 is set, which is always the case with the manual coding (0x0EC7A4/0x0F38B0, read). p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 4 to 5)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 4 to mode 5.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 5 to 4)
table.description: How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 5 to mode 4.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Fallback Latch, AT/CVT)
table.description:
Idle target ramp rate (by coolant) used when a warm-up fallback flag is set, on automatic/CVT cars.
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Used instead of the mode table when FFF899D7 bit0 rises while the idle mode is unchanged (index 98/99, 0x0F1DD0, read). FFF899D7 bit0 is the warm-up fallback latch. This one when FFF8A7E2 bit0 is clear, which happens only with the AT/CVT coding (AT state FFF8A7DD 0 or 5; 0x0EC7A4/0x0F38B0, read). p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. Confidence: read.

table.name: CAN Idle Speed Request (Alternate)
table.description:
Minimum idle speed requested by another module over CAN, by request code.
0x10EA40 (read; 20 ms task 0x1E0AE8 via 0x113060): while the network variant / frame gate holds (FFF88E0C bit 3 with FFF88621 = 1, bit 4 with FFF88618 = 1, or bit 7 with FFF88618 = 1) and FFF8A9A3 bit 0 is set, FFF8B3FA = this(CAN code FFF8A88A) for cal 0x35534 = 250 passes (5 s), then it falls by cal 0x35532 = 5 counts (1 rpm) per pass; 0 when FFF8A9A3 bit 0 clears. 0x10EB1C takes FFF854E2 = max(B3FA, a second request from FFF8A8D9 = CAN FFF88B90 + 26 scaled by cal 0x3555C, limited to cal 0x35556 = 1500 rpm), optionally remaps it through 05D3C0 / 05D3CC, and stores FFF8B3FC. FFF8B3FC's only reader is 0x0EE338, which passes it to the idle target module 0x0F2274 as stack argument 7 (disassembly at 0x0EF2E4, read); there min(B3FC, 0x1E00) >> 6 (12.5 rpm units) is maxed into a minimum idle-speed request only when param_1 = cal 0x1D0AE bit 0 and FFF8A9A2 bit 6 are both set (0x0F2826 reads @(158,R15) = param_11, read). Cal 0x1D0AE = 0, the same switch that keeps the alternate A/C idle air path and radiator-fan duty tables off. Unit: rpm x 5.12 (read from the >> 6 into 12.5 rpm units and the 0x1E00 = 1500 rpm cap). Confidence: read.

table.name: CAN Idle Speed Request Remap (Alternate)
table.description:
Remaps the CAN idle speed request before it is applied.
0x10EB1C (read, disassembly 0x10EC56-0x10EC7A): the combined request FFF854E2 (input) is passed through this table into FFF8B3FC when FFF8A7E2 bit 0 is set and FFF8A8A1 bit 7 is clear; with both set 05D3CC is used instead; with FFF8A7E2 bit 0 clear the request is stored unchanged; with FFF88B8E bit 0 (CAN 0x280) the output is cal 0x3555E (0). FFF8A7E2 bit 0 is always set on the manual coding (brief), so this is the table that would apply. Confidence: read.

table.name: CAN Idle Speed Request Remap (Flag Set, Alternate)
table.description:
Alternative remap of the CAN idle speed request, used when an unidentified CAN flag is set.
0x10EB1C (read): used instead of 05D3C0 when FFF8A8A1 bit 7 is also set; FFF8A8A1 bit 7 comes from CAN bits FFF88B95 bits 0/1 via 0x11BBB4 (read, meaning not identified). Input = combined request FFF854E2. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Mode 5)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant for normal warm idle (the warm-idle mode on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded open. At a settled warm idle the TGVs are normally commanded closed, so Idle Base Air (Mode 5, TGV Closed) is probably the table in use: change both together, and together with Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, Mode 5) so idle feedback does not have to learn the difference.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Mode 5, TGV Closed)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant for normal warm idle while the TGVs are commanded closed (the normal state at low torque, probably including warm idle). Change it together with Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, Mode 5) and Idle Base Air (Mode 5).

table.name: Idle Base Air (Post-Start, Modes 1/2)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant right after a cold start (below 75 degC) until the car moves or the engine warms, and while stopped, used while the TGVs are commanded open. Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target so idle feedback does not have to make up the difference. The TGV Closed table is used whenever the TGVs are commanded closed, which is the normal state at low torque, so change both together.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Post-Start, Modes 1/2, TGV Closed)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant right after a cold start (below 75 degC) until the car moves or the engine warms, and while stopped, used while the TGVs are commanded closed (the normal state at low torque, probably including warm idle). Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target and the normal Idle Base Air table for this mode.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Warm Start, Mode 3)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant after a hot restart (coolant at or above 75 degC at start) until the car moves, used while the TGVs are commanded open. Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target so idle feedback does not have to make up the difference. The TGV Closed table is used whenever the TGVs are commanded closed, which is the normal state at low torque, so change both together.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Warm Start, Mode 3, TGV Closed)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant after a hot restart (coolant at or above 75 degC at start) until the car moves, used while the TGVs are commanded closed (the normal state at low torque, probably including warm idle). Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target and the normal Idle Base Air table for this mode.

table.name: Idle Base Air (AT/CVT, Mode 6)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant in warm idle on automatic/CVT cars only (never used on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded open. Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target so idle feedback does not have to make up the difference. The TGV Closed table is used whenever the TGVs are commanded closed, which is the normal state at low torque, so change both together.

table.name: Idle Base Air (AT/CVT, Mode 6, TGV Closed)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant in warm idle on automatic/CVT cars only (never used on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded closed (the normal state at low torque, probably including warm idle). Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target and the normal Idle Base Air table for this mode.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Warm-Up Drive-Off, Mode 7)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant after a cold-start drive-off while the engine is still warming up, used while the TGVs are commanded open. Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target so idle feedback does not have to make up the difference. The TGV Closed table is used whenever the TGVs are commanded closed, which is the normal state at low torque, so change both together.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Warm-Up Drive-Off, Mode 7, TGV Closed)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant after a cold-start drive-off while the engine is still warming up, used while the TGVs are commanded closed (the normal state at low torque, probably including warm idle). Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target and the normal Idle Base Air table for this mode.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Warm-Up Drive-Off, AT/CVT, Mode 8)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant after a cold-start drive-off on automatic/CVT cars only (never used on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded open. Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target so idle feedback does not have to make up the difference. The TGV Closed table is used whenever the TGVs are commanded closed, which is the normal state at low torque, so change both together.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Warm-Up Drive-Off, AT/CVT, Mode 8, TGV Closed)
table.description: Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant after a cold-start drive-off on automatic/CVT cars only (never used on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded closed (the normal state at low torque, probably including warm idle). Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target and the normal Idle Base Air table for this mode.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air (Initial)
table.description: Extra idle air right after start, by start type (first start, restart, after a stall, remote start; start-type meanings inferred) and coolant. It is held after start, then decays by Post-Start Idle Air Decay once rpm reaches the idle target.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air (Initial, TGV Closed)
table.description: TGV-forced-closed version of Post-Start Idle Air (Initial): extra idle air right after start by start type and coolant, held and then decayed once rpm reaches the idle target.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air Decay
table.description: Multiplier applied every 40 ms to the post-start idle air once rpm has reached the idle target and Post-Start Idle Air Decay Delay has passed, by start type and coolant. Smaller = faster fade.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air Decay (TGV Closed)
table.description: TGV-forced-closed version of Post-Start Idle Air Decay: multiplier applied every 40 ms to the post-start idle air after the decay delay. Smaller = faster fade.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air Decay Delay
table.description: Time after start, by start type and coolant at start, before the post-start idle air starts to decay (rpm must also have reached the idle target). Longer = extra air held longer.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air Decay Delay (TGV Closed)
table.description: TGV-forced-closed version of Post-Start Idle Air Decay Delay: time after start before the post-start idle air starts to decay. Its coolant input is inferred from the sibling table.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Start Time
table.description: Time after rpm first reaches idle target when the staged air starts to rise, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air End Time
table.description: Time after rpm first reaches idle target when the staged air stops rising and starts to decay, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Level
table.description: Peak level of the staged post-start air, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Ramp Step
table.description: Rise of the staged post-start air every 40 ms between Start Time and End Time, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Decay
table.description: Multiplier applied every 40 ms after End Time, by start type and coolant (smaller = faster fade). Part of a timed post-start air bump.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Start Time (TGV Closed)
table.description: Time after rpm first reaches idle target when the staged air starts to rise, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump. TGVs-forced-closed copy; edit with the normal table.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air End Time (TGV Closed)
table.description: Time after rpm first reaches idle target when the staged air stops rising and starts to decay, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump. TGVs-forced-closed copy; edit with the normal table.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Level (TGV Closed)
table.description: Peak level of the staged post-start air, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump. TGVs-forced-closed copy; edit with the normal table.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Ramp Step (TGV Closed)
table.description: Rise of the staged post-start air every 40 ms between Start Time and End Time, by start type and coolant. Part of a timed post-start air bump. TGVs-forced-closed copy; edit with the normal table.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Decay (TGV Closed)
table.description: Multiplier applied every 40 ms after End Time, by start type and coolant (smaller = faster fade). Part of a timed post-start air bump. TGVs-forced-closed copy; edit with the normal table.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air IAT Add
table.description: Added to Post-Start Staged Air Level by intake air temperature, for the timed post-start air bump.

table.name: A/C Idle Air Steady (A/C Load Sw On, Neutral Sw Off, Above 14 km/h)
table.description: Extra idle air held while the A/C compressor is engaged, for: A/C load switch on, neutral switch off, car moving above 14 km/h. Raise if idle sags with the A/C on, lower if it flares. The A/C load switch meaning is inferred.

table.name: A/C Idle Air Initial Kick (A/C Load Sw On, Neutral Sw Off, Above 14 km/h)
table.description: Extra idle air given for the first 0.4 s after the A/C compressor engages (then it fades to the matching A/C Idle Air Steady value), for: A/C load switch on, neutral switch off, car moving above 14 km/h. Raise if idle dips when the A/C kicks in. 0 = no kick. The A/C load switch meaning is inferred.

table.name: A/C Idle Air Steady (A/C Load Sw On, Neutral Sw Off, Below 14 km/h)
table.description: Extra idle air held while the A/C compressor is engaged, for: A/C load switch on, neutral switch off, car stopped or slow. Raise if idle sags with the A/C on, lower if it flares. The A/C load switch meaning is inferred.

table.name: A/C Idle Air Initial Kick (A/C Load Sw On, Neutral Sw Off, Below 14 km/h)

table.name: Idle Air Altitude Factor (Key-On/Cranking)
table.description: Multiplier on idle air by barometric pressure, used at key-on and while cranking. The two Running copies hold the same data: edit all three together.

table.name: Idle Air Altitude Factor (Running, A/C Off)
table.description: Multiplier on idle air by barometric pressure while running with the A/C off.

table.name: Idle Air Altitude Factor (Running, A/C On)
table.description: Multiplier on idle air by barometric pressure while running with the A/C on.

table.name: Idle Air Reduction In Drive (AT/CVT, Coolant)
table.description: Idle air taken away, by coolant, while an automatic/CVT car idles in Drive (pedal released, slow) to offset the load of the transmission. Never used on a manual car.

table.name: Idle Air Reduction In Drive (AT/CVT, RPM Error)
table.description: Correction to Idle Air Reduction In Drive by rpm error (actual minus target) and coolant, for automatic/CVT cars idling in Drive. Never used on a manual car.

table.name: Minimum Idle Air (Moving in Gear)
table.description: Floor on idle air by rpm (and coolant) whenever the car is moving in gear, so the throttle cannot close below it; acts mainly as a dashpot when the pedal is released (inferred). Raise to soften throttle closing on decel; lower for faster rpm drop. Not used at standstill or in neutral.

table.name: Pull-Away Anti-Stall Air
table.description: Manual cars only: extra air, by how far rpm has dipped below a held reference, while pulling away from a standstill in gear with the pedal pressed. Raise to make launches from rest harder to stall.

table.name: Pull-Away Anti-Stall Reference Decay
table.scaling: RPM change per combustion event uint16
table.description: Manual cars only: how fast (by rpm) the reference rpm used by Pull-Away Anti-Stall Air falls per combustion event, so dips are measured from the recent peak.

table.name: Pull-Away Anti-Stall Reference Offset
table.description: Manual cars only: offset (by rpm) subtracted from the predicted reference rpm for Pull-Away Anti-Stall Air; a positive value probably means a dip must be larger before the anti-stall air reacts.

table.name: Idle RPM-Drop Recovery Air (Drop Slowing)
Y Axis
table.scaling: RPM change per combustion event int16

table.description: Extra idle air, by rpm change rate, to catch an rpm dip at idle once the drop is easing (pedal released, rpm at least 40 below target).

table.name: Idle RPM-Drop Recovery Air (Drop Continuing)
Y Axis
table.scaling: RPM change per combustion event int16

table.description: Extra idle air, by how fast rpm is falling, to catch an rpm dip at idle (pedal released, rpm at least 40 below target, at least 5 s after start). Used while the drop is not easing; see the Drop Slowing table.

table.name: Idle Air Target-Change Feed-Forward (AT/CVT, State 0/5)
table.description: Automatic/CVT version of Idle Air Target-Change Feed-Forward, used in two transmission states only: extra or less idle air applied immediately when the idle speed target changes, by the size of the step.

table.name: Idle Air Target-Change Feed-Forward
table.description: Extra (or less) idle air applied immediately when the idle speed target changes, by the size of the step, so rpm follows the new target without waiting for feedback. Positive steps add air. Used at idle on manual cars (and most automatic states).

table.name: Idle Air Trim (Charging Command)
table.description: Idle air trim by the alternator charging command. Probably compensates for lower alternator load.

table.name: Electrical Load Idle Air Hold Release (Alternator Command)
table.description: Flag table by alternator command that decides when the CAN load-value idle air adder (Idle Air Adder, CAN Load Value table) may increase while battery voltage is low.

table.name: Idle Air Adder (CAN 0x370 Load Value)
table.description: Extra idle air by a load value received over CAN, probably electrical load (not confirmed), added to the accessory idle air.

table.name: Idle Air Adder (CAN 0x280 Stage)
table.description: Extra idle air by a 3-bit stage value received over CAN, used only with one body coding. Possibly the radiator fan stage, but that is a guess.

table.name: Idle Air from Throttle Area (Torque Request)
table.description: Converts a throttle area back into idle air units when another module requests torque over CAN. Area is in mm^2 of effective throttle opening (about 2,150 mm^2 wide open).

table.name: Idle Base Air (Cold Idle, Mode 4)
table.description:
Base idle air by coolant for the cold-idle mode 4.
Details: When used: idle mode 4, entered from mode 5 when stopped with coolant below cal 0x24E94 for cal 0x24E96 passes. 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant, this table while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is clear (read). Scale as Idle Base Air (Mode 5). Raise it with this mode's idle speed target so the feedback need not cover the difference (inferred). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Cold Idle, Mode 4, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Base idle air by coolant for the cold-idle mode 4 with the TGVs commanded closed.
Details: When used: idle mode 4, entered from mode 5 when stopped with coolant below cal 0x24E94 for cal 0x24E96 passes. 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant, this table while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGV close command) is set (read). Scale as Idle Base Air (Mode 5). Raise it with this mode's idle speed target so the feedback need not cover the difference (inferred). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). FFF8A881 bit 4 is the normal TGV-close command (0x10DEFC, set mainly by the timed close request FFF8A883 bit 5 from 0x10E180 when requested torque, coolant and air flow are below the TGV thresholds; the same bit selects every TGV-closed table), not a forced or fault state (read). At a settled warm idle the request conditions hold, so the TGVs are normally commanded closed and the TGV Closed table is probably the one in use (inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air (Stop-Start Restart)
table.description: Post-start idle air for an automatic stop-start restart, by start type and coolant. the stop-start feature appears unable to activate in this calibration.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air (Stop-Start Restart, TGV Closed)
table.description: Post-start idle air for an automatic stop-start restart with the TGVs closed. the stop-start feature appears unable to activate in this calibration.

table.name: A/C Idle Air (Alternate, Target RPM)
table.description: A/C idle air by an unidentified CAN load value and idle target rpm, for an alternate A/C idle-air path.

table.name: A/C Idle Air (Alternate, Engine Speed)
table.description: A/C idle air by an unidentified CAN load value and engine speed, for an alternate A/C idle-air path.

table.name: A/C Idle Air Initial Kick (Alternate)
table.description:
Initial A/C idle air kick by an unidentified CAN code, for an alternate A/C idle-air path.
Details: When used: with cal 0x1D0AE bit 0 set, while FFF8A9A3 bit 0 is set and the time since it was set is below A/C Idle Air Kick Duration: kick = this(FFF8A88A), afterwards the kick falls by cal 0x3539C (23) per 10 ms (0x0EC10C, read). FFF8A88A is a 0..6 code from received bits FFF88B8D 5-7 (CAN 0x280 byte 4 bits 5-7; 0x10E8C4 / 0x10E9C0, read; meaning not identified). Alternate A/C idle-air path of 0x0EC10C (10 ms idle module 0x0EE338; call checked in the disassembly). The sibling 2D tables' row input FFF8A8C6 (not used by this table) = cal 0x3555C (121) x received byte FFF88B91 (CAN 0x280 byte 5) / 100, capped at cal 0x35A84 (128), or cal 0x35A85 when FFF88B8E bit 0 (0x115F80, read); filtered by cal 0x353C1 while A/C (A9A3 bit 0) is on. Its physical meaning is not identified (A/C load related, inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: A/C Idle Air Kick Duration (Alternate)
table.description:
How long the alternate A/C idle air kick is held, by an unidentified CAN code.
Details: When used: with cal 0x1D0AE bit 0 set: the A/C idle-air kick (A/C Idle Air Initial Kick (Alternate)) is held while the 10 ms pass count since FFF8A9A3 bit 0 was set is below this(FFF8A88A) (0x0EC10C, read); FFF8A88A is a 0..6 code from received bits FFF88B8D 5-7 (CAN 0x280 byte 4; meaning not identified). Alternate A/C idle-air path of 0x0EC10C (10 ms idle module 0x0EE338; call checked in the disassembly). The sibling 2D tables' row input FFF8A8C6 (not used by this table) = cal 0x3555C (121) x received byte FFF88B91 (CAN 0x280 byte 5) / 100, capped at cal 0x35A84 (128), or cal 0x35A85 when FFF88B8E bit 0 (0x115F80, read); filtered by cal 0x353C1 while A/C (A9A3 bit 0) is on. Its physical meaning is not identified (A/C load related, inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: Low Voltage Idle Request Threshold (Alternator Command)
table.description: Battery voltage threshold, by alternator command, for a low-voltage idle-up request. Unused in this ROM: its result is never read, so editing it has no effect.

table.name: Idle Speed Feedback Map (Target MAP Offset)
Y Axis
table.scaling: RPM change per combustion event int16

table.description: Probably the main idle speed feedback map: how much the target manifold pressure (air) is raised or cut, by rpm error from the idle target and how fast rpm is changing. Positive = more air. Larger values give a stronger correction but risk hunting. Only active while idle feedback is on.

table.name: Idle Speed Feedback RPM Error Factor (Above Target)
table.description: Scales the rpm error used by the idle feedback when rpm is above the idle target. Lower values make the feedback react less to overshoot.

table.name: Idle Speed Feedback Gain Multiplier (Time in Feedback)
table.description: Multiplier on both idle feedback gains by how long idle feedback has been running with rpm near target.

table.name: Idle Speed Torque Feedback P
table.description: Torque correction (ft-lb) for idle speed by idle target and rpm error (positive = engine too slow), used when idle is held by torque control (inferred), within about 500 rpm of the idle target.

table.name: Idle Speed Torque Feedback D
table.description: Torque correction (ft-lb) for idle speed by idle target and how fast rpm changed over the last 20 ms; damps rpm swings when idle is held by torque control (inferred), within about 500 rpm of the idle target.

table.name: Idle Speed Torque Feedback Reference Torque
table.description: Reference torque by rpm that scales the idle torque feedback (P and D): a larger value gives a smaller correction. Must not be set to 0 ft-lb, which zeroes the feedback.

table.name: Idle Feedback Carry-Over Decay (Positive)
table.scaling: idle air (base-air units) per 10 ms uint16

table.name: Y Axis
table.scaling: RPM change per combustion event int16

table.description: How fast the idle feedback air kept when leaving idle is bled off, by rpm change rate; this acts like a dashpot (inferred). Larger = faster release.

table.name: Idle Feedback Carry-Over Decay (Negative)
table.scaling: idle air (base-air units) per 10 ms uint16

table.name: Y Axis
table.scaling: RPM change per combustion event int16

table.description: How fast a negative leftover of idle feedback air is released after leaving idle, by rpm change rate. Larger = cancels sooner.

table.name: Idle Feedback Carry-Over Limit (Positive)
table.description: Limit on a positive idle-feedback carry-over, as a fraction by throttle opening above idle. The carried-over air keeps the air idle feedback had added when leaving idle and releases it gradually (dashpot-like, inferred).

table.name: Idle Feedback Carry-Over Limit (Negative)
table.description: Limit on a negative idle-feedback carry-over, as a fraction by throttle opening above idle. The carried-over air keeps the air idle feedback had added when leaving idle and releases it gradually (dashpot-like, inferred).

table.name: Idle Converter Slip Threshold (In Gear, AT/CVT)
table.description: Automatic/CVT only: converter slip, by coolant, needed for the ECU to treat the car as stopped in gear for idle control (probably torque-converter slip). Never used on a manual car.

table.name: Idle Converter Slip Threshold (Neutral, AT/CVT)
table.description: Automatic/CVT only: converter slip, by coolant, needed for the ECU to treat the car as in neutral/park for idle control (probably torque-converter slip). Never used on a manual car.

table.name: Idle Learn Filter Gain (Before First Transfer)
table.description: Long-term idle learning speed used after an idle-learn reset until the first learned value has been stored.

table.name: Idle Learn Filter Gain (A/C Off)
table.description: How fast the long-term idle air learning follows the current correction with the A/C off, by time since the last learning transfer. Larger = learns faster but less stable.

table.name: Idle Learn Filter Gain (A/C On)
table.description: How fast the long-term idle air learning follows the current correction with the A/C on, by time since the last learning transfer. Larger = learns faster but less stable.

table.name: Idle Learn Bias Index Step
table.description: How the drive-history index for Idle Learn Bias moves every 2 s, by vehicle speed (only with coolant at or above 80 degC).

table.name: Idle Learn Bias
table.description: Offset added to the long-term idle air learning by a drive-history index: long idling pushes the learned idle air down, sustained driving pushes it up (purpose, e.g. heat soak, inferred). Index movement is set by Idle Learn Bias Index Step.

table.name: EGR Target Rate (TGV Open)
table.description: Main EGR rate target (% of intake charge, probably external EGR) by rpm and load while the TGVs are open. 0 = no EGR. Capped by EGR Target Rate Maximum.

table.name: EGR Target Rate (TGV Closed)
table.description: Main EGR rate target (% of intake charge, probably external EGR) by rpm and load while the TGVs are closed. 0 = no EGR. Raising it adds more exhaust gas at light load. Capped by EGR Target Rate Maximum.

table.name: EGR Target Rate Maximum
table.description: Hard cap on the target EGR rate.

table.name: EGR Target Rate Coolant Multiplier
table.description: Multiplier (255 = 1.0) by coolant on the target EGR rate.

table.name: EGR Target Rate DAM Multiplier
table.description: Multiplier (128 = 1.0) on the target EGR rate by the knock learning value (probably DAM).

table.name: EGR Target Rate Reduction Multiplier
table.description: Multiplier (255 = 1.0) by rpm and load that reduces the target EGR rate while an unidentified module requests it and EGR flow is present. When the request is active is not known.

table.name: EGR Enable Minimum Air after Start
table.description: Amount of air (probably the air drawn since start), by coolant at start, that must pass before EGR is enabled.

table.name: EGR Enable Coolant Minimum
table.description: EGR is only enabled when coolant is at or above this.

table.name: EGR Enable Coolant Maximum
table.description: EGR is only enabled when coolant is at or below this.

table.name: EGR Enable RPM Minimum
table.description: EGR is only enabled when rpm is at or above this.

table.name: EGR Enable RPM Maximum
table.description: EGR is only enabled when rpm is at or below this.

table.name: EGR Enable Load Minimum
table.description: EGR is only enabled when load is at or above this.

table.name: EGR Enable Load Maximum
table.description: EGR is only enabled when load is at or below this.

table.name: EGR Enable Intake Air Temp Minimum
table.description: EGR is only enabled when intake air temperature is at or above this.

table.name: EGR Enable Battery Voltage Minimum
table.description: EGR is only enabled when battery voltage is at or above this.

table.name: EGR Enable Vehicle Speed Minimum
table.description: EGR is only enabled when the car is moving at least this fast (vehicle speed signal inferred).

table.name: EGR Enable Exhaust Pressure Margin
table.description: EGR is only enabled when the estimated pressure upstream of the EGR valve exceeds manifold pressure by at least this much, so exhaust gas can actually flow.

table.name: EGR Active Threshold
table.description: Target EGR rate above which EGR counts as active, which switches ignition to the Base Timing (EGR Active) tables. See EGR Active Threshold Hysteresis for the switch-off point.

table.name: EGR Active Threshold Hysteresis
table.description: How far below EGR Active Threshold the target EGR rate must fall before EGR counts as inactive again.

table.name: EGR Timing Advance (TGV Closed)
table.description: Extra timing advance requested while EGR is active with the TGVs closed, by rpm and load, scaled by how much EGR is flowing. It is added to the Primary Ignition request, so it reaches the spark only where that request (plus knock advance) is below the Base Timing (EGR Active) map, never above it.

table.name: EGR Timing Advance (TGV Open)
table.description: Extra timing advance requested while EGR is active with the TGVs open, by rpm and load, scaled by how much EGR is flowing. It is added to the Primary Ignition request, so it reaches the spark only where that request (plus knock advance) is below the Base Timing (EGR Active) map, never above it.

table.name: EGR Coolant Timing Adjustment (TGV Closed)
table.description: Timing adjustment by rpm and load while EGR is active and the TGVs are closed, scaled by EGR Coolant Timing Adjustment Coolant Multiplier so it acts only on a cooler engine. It is added to both base timing and the timing request, so it moves the fired timing directly.

table.name: EGR Coolant Timing Adjustment Coolant Multiplier
table.description: Multiplier (255 = 1.0) by coolant on the EGR timing adjustment tables.

table.name: EGR Target Flow Coolant Multiplier
table.description: Multiplier (128 = 1.0) by coolant and load on the target EGR flow that drives the valve.

table.name: EGR Valve Position from Target Flow
table.description: Feed-forward EGR valve position (steps) for a target EGR flow; feedback is added on top.

table.name: EGR Valve Flow Model
table.description: Estimated EGR flow by pressure difference across the valve and valve position. Used both for the actual EGR flow estimate and for the flow feedback, so edits change both.

table.name: EGR Valve Flow Feedback Integral Step
table.description: How fast the EGR valve feedback corrects position, by the error between target and modelled flow. Positive opens the valve. Larger = faster correction, more risk of hunting.

table.name: EGR Valve Feedback Integral Minimum
table.description: Lower limit of the EGR valve flow-feedback correction (how far feedback may close the valve below feed-forward).

table.name: EGR Valve Feedback Integral Maximum
table.description: Upper limit of the EGR valve flow-feedback correction (how far feedback may open the valve beyond feed-forward).

table.name: EGR Upstream Pressure Estimate
table.description: Estimated pressure upstream of the EGR valve (probably exhaust side) by rpm and load. The difference to manifold pressure sets the modelled EGR flow and decides whether EGR may be enabled.

table.name: EGR Upstream Pressure Estimate (Blend Partner)
table.description: Second EGR upstream pressure estimate, blended in only while a flag is set that is probably 'TGVs closed' (inferred).

table.name: EGR Upstream Pressure Baro Adder
table.description: Correction by rpm and load added to EGR Upstream Pressure Estimate, scaled by EGR Upstream Pressure Baro Adder Multiplier.

table.name: EGR Upstream Pressure Baro Adder Multiplier
table.description: Multiplier (128 = 1.0) by barometric pressure on EGR Upstream Pressure Baro Adder.

table.name: EGR Target Rate (TGV Open, Multi-Injection)
table.description:
EGR rate target by rpm and load with the TGVs open and multiple injections per cycle.
Details: When used: TGVs not closed and multi-injection active (FFF8A775 bit 1); cal 0x2F797 bit 5 clear. Base target EGR rate A818, looked up by 0x0FA10C with rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8A616 (read, disassembly). Target EGR rate (0x0FA260, read): FFF8A81A = base A817 x Coolant Multiplier 05CB04/255 x 255/255 (A816) x Reduction Multiplier A81C/255 x DAM Multiplier 05CB10/128, x 640 (1/640 units), capped at cal 0x2C4E6 (192 = 30 %) and forced to 0 unless the enable conditions FFF8A811 bit 0 hold (0x0FAAFC). A817 follows the base table A818 (0x0FA068). Multi-injection = FFF8A775 bit 1, set by 0x0FAABC when the multi-injection enable FFF8A775 bit 0 is set and all four per-injector strategy bytes FFF8A69F..A6A2 are 2 or 3 (read). TGVs closed = FFF8A881 bit 4 set (read: 0x10C948 drives the TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 to 0 while the bit is set). EGR controller task 0x0F94A8 (read). That this is external EGR is inferred: its commanded output FFF8A81B is the OBD PID 0x2C (Commanded EGR) source and FFF88A1C (actual position) feeds PID 0x2D (EGR error) (0x1717C8, 0x1715F0, read). 0 = no EGR. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: EGR Target Rate (TGV Closed, Multi-Injection)
table.description:
EGR rate target by rpm and load with the TGVs closed and multiple injections per cycle.
Details: When used: TGVs closed and multi-injection active (FFF8A775 bit 1); cal 0x2F797 bit 5 clear. Base target EGR rate A818, looked up by 0x0FA10C with rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8A616 (read, disassembly). Target EGR rate (0x0FA260, read): FFF8A81A = base A817 x Coolant Multiplier 05CB04/255 x 255/255 (A816) x Reduction Multiplier A81C/255 x DAM Multiplier 05CB10/128, x 640 (1/640 units), capped at cal 0x2C4E6 (192 = 30 %) and forced to 0 unless the enable conditions FFF8A811 bit 0 hold (0x0FAAFC). A817 follows the base table A818 (0x0FA068). Multi-injection = FFF8A775 bit 1, set by 0x0FAABC when the multi-injection enable FFF8A775 bit 0 is set and all four per-injector strategy bytes FFF8A69F..A6A2 are 2 or 3 (read). TGVs closed = FFF8A881 bit 4 set (read: 0x10C948 drives the TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 to 0 while the bit is set). EGR controller task 0x0F94A8 (read). That this is external EGR is inferred: its commanded output FFF8A81B is the OBD PID 0x2C (Commanded EGR) source and FFF88A1C (actual position) feeds PID 0x2D (EGR error) (0x1717C8, 0x1715F0, read). 0 = no EGR. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: EGR Target Rate (Alternate, TGV Open)
table.description:
Alternate EGR rate target by rpm and throttle position (instead of load) with the TGVs open.
Details: When used: only when cal 0x2F797 bit 5 is set. Alternate base target EGR rate A818 (0x0FA10C, read), indexed by rpm FFF8CD54 and throttle position FFF8CD77 (about 0.56 % per count, see below) instead of load. Target EGR rate (0x0FA260, read): FFF8A81A = base A817 x Coolant Multiplier 05CB04/255 x 255/255 (A816) x Reduction Multiplier A81C/255 x DAM Multiplier 05CB10/128, x 640 (1/640 units), capped at cal 0x2C4E6 (192 = 30 %) and forced to 0 unless the enable conditions FFF8A811 bit 0 hold (0x0FAAFC). A817 follows the base table A818 (0x0FA068). TGVs closed = FFF8A881 bit 4 set (read: 0x10C948 drives the TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 to 0 while the bit is set). EGR controller task 0x0F94A8 (read). That this is external EGR is inferred: its commanded output FFF8A81B is the OBD PID 0x2C (Commanded EGR) source and FFF88A1C (actual position) feeds PID 0x2D (EGR error) (0x1717C8, 0x1715F0, read). p16 (read): second axis FFF8CD77 = (ETC throttle position FFF8A342 - 10)/4 = (ETC actual position FFF8A2B6 - 1000)/256 (0x09D58E, 0x09DAAE, 0x0A0680, 0x06AB94): a throttle-position byte, about 0.56 % per count (inferred). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: EGR Target Rate (Alternate, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Alternate EGR rate target by rpm and throttle position (instead of load) with the TGVs closed.
Details: When used: only when cal 0x2F797 bit 5 is set. Alternate base target EGR rate A818 (0x0FA10C, read), indexed by rpm FFF8CD54 and throttle position FFF8CD77 (about 0.56 % per count, see below) instead of load. Target EGR rate (0x0FA260, read): FFF8A81A = base A817 x Coolant Multiplier 05CB04/255 x 255/255 (A816) x Reduction Multiplier A81C/255 x DAM Multiplier 05CB10/128, x 640 (1/640 units), capped at cal 0x2C4E6 (192 = 30 %) and forced to 0 unless the enable conditions FFF8A811 bit 0 hold (0x0FAAFC). Confidence: inferred.
